## What is Crohn’s disease?
Crohn’s disease is one of the two main forms of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD).
Crohn’s disease is believed to be caused by an overactive immune response which results in inflammation within the digestive system.
Think you might be experiencing Crohn’s disease
Most commonly, the inflammation within the digestive system which occurs in Crohn’s disease affects sections of the terminal ileum ‒ the final segment of the small intestine ‒ and/or the colon ‒ the large intestine ‒ but it can affect any of the gastrointestinal organs.
Crohn’s disease usually develops in adulthood but can, in some cases, manifest in childhood or adolescence. [1](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") It is a lifelong, chronic condition.
People affected by Crohn’s disease experience periods of:
  * Remission, in which the disease is inactive and the individual is without symptoms
  * Flare-ups, in which the disease is active and symptoms are present


Treatment for Crohn’s disease aims to alleviate the symptoms and prolong periods of remission.
## Crohn’s disease Symptoms
A person who is affected by Crohn’s disease may experience a wide range of symptoms which may also vary in severity.
Common symptoms of Crohn’s disease[2](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2")
### 1. Digestive discomfort
This takes the form of abdominal pain and cramping and often occurs one or two hours after eating, but may occur at any time. People with Crohn’s disease often avoid eating or eat less in order to avoid digestive discomfort, which can lead to weight loss. Digestive discomfort is usually at its worst when an individual is experiencing a flare-up of the disease. [3](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3")
### 2. Diarrhea
This is one of the main symptoms of Crohn’s disease and happens when the gut cannot absorb all the necessary fluid from food during the digestive process. This often creates a sense of urgency and needing to rush to the toilet. 
### 3. Fatigue
A high percentage of people with Crohn’s disease are affected by fatigue. [5](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:5 "See Footnote 5") This may be caused by lack of sleep[6](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6")
Fatigue may also be caused by malnutrition[vitamin B12](https://ada.com/micronutrients/vitamin-b12/) and vitamin D. [7](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:7 "See Footnote 7") These deficiencies often correlate to a loss in muscle strength. [8](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:8 "See Footnote 8") If you or a loved one is feeling tired for unknown reasons, you get a free symptom assessment by downloading the 
### 4. Blood in one’s stools
Crohn’s disease typically causes bleeding in the lower digestive tract, which manifests as bright red blood in one’s stools. The condition may also cause bleeding in the colon, associated with inflammation, [anal fissures](https://ada.com/conditions/anal-fissure/) and fistulas. [9](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:9 "See Footnote 9")
### 5. Mucus in one’s stools
A healthy intestine produces a certain amount of mucus in order to protect and lubricate the bowel area. When a person is affected by Crohn’s disease, the production of mucus can increase, resulting in surplus mucus emerging with one’s stools. This usually takes the form of a gel-like material which appears to coat the stool. [10](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:10 "See Footnote 10")
### 6. Unintentional weight loss
Due to avoiding certain foods or food groups and failing to absorb sufficient energy from one’s food as a result of malabsorption and diarrhea, people with Crohn’s disease frequently experience weight loss.
### 7. Other symptoms
Less common symptoms[2](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2")
  * Nausea and vomiting
  * High temperature and/or being prone to fevers
  * Swelling and pain in the joints
  * Mouth ulcers
  * Skin irritation involving redness, swelling and itching
  * Uveitis, i.e. red and irritated eyes


Think you might be experiencing Crohn’s disease symptoms
## Crohn’s disease Causes
Approximately 1.6 million people in the U.S. are affected by either Crohn’s disease or ulcerative colitis, the other prominent form of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). [11](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:11 "See Footnote 11") The exact reasons why Crohn’s disease develops in people are unknown
When it encounters environmental or genetic factors or a combination of the two, the immune system can be triggered, resulting in the inflammation associated with Crohn’s disease.
Foreign substances (antigens) which one encounters, particularly those related to smoking tobacco and to one’s diet, may irritate and cause inflammation in the intestines, resulting in the development of Crohn’s disease. Alternatively, these stimuli may correlate to an autoimmune response, whereby the body’s immune system causes areas of the gastrointestinal system to become inflamed.
## Crohn’s disease risk factors
Anyone can be affected by Crohn’s disease, but it is most likely to manifest in people between the ages of 10 and 40.
Factors which increase one’s risk of experiencing Crohn’s disease include:
  * Being of European descent, in particular of Ashkenazi Jewish origin) [12](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:12 "See Footnote 12")
  * Smoking tobacco [13](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:13 "See Footnote 13")
  * Being female [14](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:14 "See Footnote 14")
  * Genetic factors; having an affected family member is a significant risk factor


## Crohn's disease diagnosis
People often experience the symptoms of Crohn’s disease for many years before being diagnosed with the condition. In order to establish a diagnosis of Crohn’s disease, doctors will consider a person’s medical history and symptoms and will also perform a physical examination.
Diagnostic techniques for Crohn’s disease include:[15](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:15 "See Footnote 15")
### 1. Medical history survey
Doctors will make a full survey of the affected person’s medical history, including when their symptoms began, their dietary habits, use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), history of smoking and whether they have a family history of Crohn’s disease or inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Doctors will pay particular attention to noting whether they have been affected by appendicitis.
### 2. Physical examination
This will take into account an individual’s height, weight, sex, blood pressure, body mass index (BMI), and will include a digital-rectal examination, an examination of the abdomen, as well as a survey of the eyes, joints, heartbeat, lungs, back, pulse, and the skin and muscles, where extraintestinal symptoms of Crohn’s disease may be found.
### 3. Laboratory studies
These will be performed in order to test one’s levels of electrolytes and creatinine, and a [bilirubin](https://ada.com/biomarkers/bilirubin/), transferrin vitamin B12 and folic acid.
Doctors will also prescribe tests to determine the individual’s erythrocyte sedimentation rate (the rate at which red blood cells coagulate), liver function tests and a urine strip to test for irregularities in the content of their urine.
### 4. Imaging studies
Imaging techniques such as MRI and CT scans will be used to screen extraintestinal symptoms such as fistulas, abscesses or sclerosing cholangitis (liver disease). People who are suspected of having Crohn’s disease will often undergo an ileocolonoscopy, in which a tube-like device containing a camera is passed through the colon in order to examine the ileum, and/or an esophagogastroduodenoscopy, in which the tube-like device is swallowed in order to examine problems relating to the upper gastrointestinal tract.
If it is not possible to scan the terminal ileum using conventional imaging studies, a wireless capsule endoscopy[16](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:16 "See Footnote 16")
### 5. Biopsy samples
Biopsy samples will be taken from at least five segments of the gastrointestinal tract will be taken during the esophagogastroduodenoscopy in order to investigate the extent of the inflammation, and the inflammatory cell infiltrate, lymphocytes and plasma cells.
### 6. Stool samples
Stool samples will be taken to test for the presence of bacteria called Clostridium difficile, which cause diarrhea and gastrointestinal conditions.
### 7. Microbial studies
These studies will be performed via stool samples to identify the microorganisms, including pathogens and members of the indigenous microbiota, which may be present in an individual’s gastrointestinal system and which may initiate or propagate the inflammatory process characteristic of Crohn’s disease. [17](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:17 "See Footnote 17")
The testing process to determine a definitive diagnosis of Crohn’s disease is thorough. This is due to the fact that the condition is one of many, which are associated with pain and cramping in the abdomen.
### 7. Differential diagnosis
Conditions which are often confused with Crohn’s disease, and which will be ruled out during the course of the diagnostic process include:
  * Stomach ulcers
  * [Gastritis (stomach irritation)](https://ada.com/conditions/chronic-gastritis/)
  * [Irritable bowel syndrome](https://ada.com/conditions/irritable-bowel-syndrome/) (IBS), which has similar symptoms to Crohn’s disease, but is a much less serious condition, which does not result in damage to the intestine
  * Gastrointestinal reflux disease (GERD)
  * [Appendicitis](https://ada.com/conditions/acute-appendicitis/)
  * [Ulcerative colitis](https://ada.com/conditions/ulcerative-colitis/), the other main form of inflammatory bowel disease


The final step in the diagnosis of Crohn’s disease involves collecting information to devise a treatment plan for the affected individual. This assessment will be performed by a doctor specialising in diseases of the gastrointestinal tract, called a gastroenterologist.
This initial assessment will establish: [18](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:18 "See Footnote 18")
  * The extent of the disease
  * Complications such as fistulae and stricturing
  * Nutritional status and deficiencies
  * Bone density and the corresponding risk of conditions such as osteoporosis


If you are worried that you or someone you know may have this condition, use the symptom checker works.
## Crohn's disease treatment
There is currently no cure for Crohn’s disease, but there are many treatment options available to alleviate the symptoms
  * Treating the symptoms
  * Minimising flare ups
  * Maintaining periods of remission


With effective treatment, many people with Crohn’s disease will experience significant periods, possibly several years, without symptoms. For people with more severe forms of the condition, and for whom medications do not provide significant relief from the symptoms, surgery may be required.
### Steroid medication
Initial treatment of Crohn’s disease will usually involve the prescription of steroid medications (corticosteroids), which are used to reduce inflammation.
However, long-term usage of corticosteroids is associated with problematic side effects
  * Swelling of the face
  * Unwanted weight gain
  * Increased susceptibility to infections
  * Bone density loss and resultant osteoporosis


When a person embarks on a course of corticosteroid medication, an aim of this treatment will usually be to reduce the dose over time, so as to minimise one’s exposure to harmful side effects.
Good to know:
### Polymeric diet
For individuals, whose growth and development may have been affected by Crohn’s disease, a polymeric (liquid) diet administered through a nasogastric tube may be recommended as an initial treatment. Many studies have been undertaken, comparing the polymeric diet to steroid medication, and it is considered an equally effective first-line treatment for Crohn’s disease. [20](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:20 "See Footnote 20")
A polymeric diet will be prescribed in order to allow the digestive system to recover[20](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:20 "See Footnote 20")
A person who has been prescribed a polymeric diet will progress to slowly reintroducing solid foods into their diet in a controlled setting, in order to safeguard the period of remission facilitated by undertaking the liquid diet. 
### Immunosuppressants
If a person, who is being treated with corticosteroids or the polymeric diet, experiences a flare up of their symptoms twice or more during one year, or finds that they return when their steroid dose is reduced, medicines which suppress the immune system (immunosuppressants) may be prescribed in combination with the initial course of treatment.
The immunosuppressant medications which are most commonly prescribed for the treatment of Crohn’s disease are azathioprine and mercaptopurine. They work by damping down the over-activity of the cells within the immune system. Methotrexate is not recommended for use during pregnancy.
It is vital that a blood test is performed before immunosuppressant medication is prescribed.[23](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:23 "See Footnote 23")
People who are using immunosuppressant medication in the treatment of Crohn’s disease will undergo regular blood tests in order to ensure that the medication continues to agree with them, so that their use can be discontinued if needed, averting the presence of unwanted side effects.Possible side effects of immunosuppressant medication include:
  * Nausea and vomiting
  * Susceptibility to infection
  * Inflammation of the pancreas (pancreatitis)
  * Liver problems
  * [Anemia](https://ada.com/conditions/anemia/), characterised by feeling tired, breathless and weak


### Biologic therapies
Biologic therapies are a type of immunosuppressant medications which use substances, such as antibodies and enzymes, to inhibit the effects of Crohn’s disease.
The development of biologic therapies therefore presents a breakthrough alternative treatment option for those who are unwilling or unable to use steroid medication. Historically, people with Crohn’s disease and other types of IBD faced a lack of effective treatment options. Corticosteroid therapy does not alleviate the symptoms of Crohn’s disease in all cases and for those whose symptoms do not respond to it, prolonged systemic corticosteroid therapy and surgery were previously the only options. [24](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:24 "See Footnote 24")
If a person responds well to biologic therapy, its benefits may include:
  * Removal of the need to use steroid medication, thereby avoiding its side effects
  * Prolonged periods in which the disease is in remission
  * Potential delay or negation of the need for surgery to redress intestinal damage caused by Crohn’s disease


### Why is biologic therapy not always offered as a first-line treatment?
Medical opinion is divided as to whether biologic therapies should be a first-line treatment option, and many doctors prefer to investigate whether a case of Crohn’s disease can be treated with corticosteroids, a liquid diet or traditional immunosuppressants initially, before considering biologic therapy.
The principal reason that some doctors prefer to prescribe traditional treatment methods first is that less is understood about the mechanism of action of biologic medications, and how different people will respond to them. Allergic reactions to the medications used in biologic therapies may occur
### Methods of administration
The two medications used in biologic therapy for Crohn’s disease are Infliximab and Adalimumab.
These medications are considered to be broadly comparable in terms of their effectiveness in bringing about prolonged periods of remission and preventing the development of complications, such as intestinal obstructions, which require surgery. [25](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:25 "See Footnote 25") Both children and adults can be prescribed Infliximab but Adalimumab is only suitable for adults.
Both medications are usually prescribed on a twelve month course.
Infliximab is administered as an infusion
Adalimumab can be administered as an injection
### Surgery
The type of surgical procedure which will be prescribed in this case is called a resection. Doctors will consider performing a resection to remove the inflamed sections of the intestinal tract in cases where the symptoms of Crohn’s disease have not been alleviated by other treatments.
A resection is a major procedure
#### Ileostomy (temporary or permanent)
An ileostomy is a procedure which involves diverting one’s digestive waste away from the colon in order to give the area, which has undergone a resection, a chance to heal. [26](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:26 "See Footnote 26") This can be temporary or permanent.
The type of ileostomy prescribed as an adjunct to a resection is usually a loop ileostomy, a temporary version of ileostomy, performed under general anaesthetic, which will be reversed after the body has had a chance to recover from undergoing resection surgery. [27](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:27 "See Footnote 27")
In a loop ileostomy, an opening in the lower abdominal area, called a stoma, is surgically created. An ileostomy bag, also called a [colostomy bag](https://ada.com/colostomy-bag/) or pouch, is then attached to the small intestine through the stoma. The bag hangs outside the body and collects the waste products that would otherwise have passed into one’s large intestine and out of one’s rectum. [27](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:27 "See Footnote 27") Normal function of the digestive system will be restored when the ileostomy is reversed.
A loop ileostomy is not always necessary as an accompaniment to a resection. One’s physician will advise on whether the procedure is needed.
## Crohn's disease self-care
A person's lifestyle, exercise routine and diet plan will generally need to be tailored to their individual needs as determined by their condition, and may need to be adjusted according to their symptoms.
Managing Crohn’s disease can involve:
  * Maintaining periods of remission
  * Making lifestyle adjustments to accommodate medical appointments
  * Management of pain and digestive discomfort
  * Co-ordinating an appropriate lifestyle whilst undergoing treatment
  * Surgery aftercare


Changing one’s diet after surgery may be necessary.The likelihood of a person developing problems associated with malabsorption increases, the more intestinal tissue is removed.
In order to ensure that the affected person receives as much nutritional benefit from their food as possible, doctors will advise on the most appropriate food plan for each person, in order to reduce the chances of vitamin and mineral deficiencies after surgery.
### Lifestyle adaptations
Crohn’s disease is a chronic condition, which means that one must make certain adjustments to one’s lifestyle,
People with Crohn’s disease will undergo periods when they need to attend frequent medical appointments
Travelling with Crohn’s disease
Knowing the location of nearby restrooms
### Exercise
It is important for everybody to engage in a certain amount of physical activity in order to maintain a healthy body. This includes people who are affected by Crohn’s disease. However, inflammation, fatigue and urgency are all factors which mean that an individual with Crohn’s disease will need to identify the appropriate fitness plan for them. Physical activity which is too intense may exacerbate the inflammation in people affected by Crohn’s disease.
There has not been significant research into the ideal types and intensities of physical activity for different levels of severity of Crohn’s disease. However, a recent review of current research suggests that a personalized exercise plan would be ideal. [28](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:28 "See Footnote 28")
This should be devised taking into account factors such as: [28](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:28 "See Footnote 28")
  * Age
  * Fitness level
  * Exercise goals
  * Preferences
  * Severity of one’s Crohn’s disease and associated needs, such as proximity to restrooms


The types of activity which have been found convenient and helpful for people with Crohn’s disease, include: [28](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:28 "See Footnote 28")
  * Aerobic activity, especially walking
  * Muscular resistance training, which can be carried out at home, if necessary


### Diet
There is currently no dietary template to follow in order to minimize the symptoms of Crohn’s disease. Individuals react differently to different foodstuffs, and everybody will find it helpful to avoid particular foods, which appear to aggravate their symptoms.
However, there are some general principles which are widely acknowledged to be helpful in preventing flare-ups of Crohn’s disease symptoms, including:
  * Eating smaller meals which are easier to digest
  * Drinking plenty of water
  * Keeping a food diary to ensure a balanced diet and to track adverse reactions to particular foods
  * Monitoring one’s fiber intake to discern whether high-fiber products trigger one’s symptoms
  * Choosing low-fat products
  * Avoiding foods which produce excessive bloating and gas


## Complications from Crohn’s disease
In addition to experiencing the immediate symptoms of Crohn’s disease, people with the condition are also predisposed to further health complications.Related conditions which commonly affect people with Crohn’s disease include:
### Intestinal obstruction
This condition is also referred to as bowel obstruction. Over time, the inflammation of the digestive tract in people with Crohn’s disease can cause the wall of the affected area(s) of the small or large intestine to thicken permanently. This can cause the intestine to become blocked. Intestinal obstructions can be fatal if left untreated and often require surgical removal. [29](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:29 "See Footnote 29")
### Anal fissure
This is a tear or sore which can occur in the anal canal. Anal fissures are common in people with Crohn’s disease, due to the trauma which is caused to the area by frequent bowel movements. [30](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:30 "See Footnote 30")
### Anal abscess
An anal abscess is an infected cavity filled with pus. Abscesses can affect the anus or rectum as a result of the internal glands in the anus becoming infected. This is likely to occur in people with Crohn’s disease, as the tissue in this area is often traumatized due to frequent bowel movements. [31](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:31 "See Footnote 31")
### Fistulae
The inflammation caused by Crohn’s disease often creates ulcers, leaks and abscesses in the bowel wall. The more severe the inflammation, the more likely it is that one of these abrasions will develop into a hole, which then forms a fistula. A fistula is a tunnel[32](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:32 "See Footnote 32")
The larger a fistula is, the more likely it is to become infected. This can cause problems like irritation of the skin and leakage of feces into or from the space which has been connected to the bowel. [32](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:32 "See Footnote 32") If you suspect you may have this condition, you can get a free symptom assessment by downloading the 
### Iron deficiency anaemia
This condition often occurs in people with Crohn’s disease, due to the bleeding in the digestive tract, and because malabsorption can cause a person’s iron levels to become deficient. It is associated with shortness of breath, fatigue and a pale complexion. [33](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:33 "See Footnote 33")
[Read more about Ireon Deficiency Anemia »](https://ada.com/conditions/iron-deficiency-anemia/)
### Osteoporosis
Osteoporosis is a disorder of the skeleton, in which the structure of the bones becomes porous. This can lead to the bones becoming weak, fragile and prone to painful fractures (breaks). In people with Crohn’s disease, osteoporosis can occur due to the intestines failing to absorb sufficient nutrients to support healthy bone growth, or due to the use of steroid medication, which may be used in the treatment of Crohn’s disease.
[Read more about Osteoporosis »](https://ada.com/conditions/osteoporosis/)
### Vitamin B12 deficiency
Often signalled by fatigue and a lack of energy, vitamin B12 deficiency is likely to occur in people with Crohn’s disease due to malabsorption.
[Read more about Vitamin B12 Deficiency »](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/)
### Pyoderma gangrenosum
This is a treatable, non-infectious skin condition, [34](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:34 "See Footnote 34") characterised by painful ulcers, which typically develop purple or blue edges, and may ooze fluid. They most commonly occur on the legs.
### Hypercoagulability
People affected by Crohn’s disease are at an increased risk of blood clots forming, which may result in deep vein thrombosis (DVT) or a pulmonary embolism if left untreated. The link between hypercoagulability and Crohn’s disease is not yet fully understood, but recent research suggests that imbalances between the levels of clotting and thinning agents in the blood caused by inflammation from Crohn’s disease, contributes to the development of the condition. [35](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:35 "See Footnote 35")
### Colorectal cancer
People whose Crohn’s disease affects their colon have a slightly increased risk of developing colorectal cancer. It is advisable to attend regular checkups and to undergo a colonoscopy to screen for colon cancer.
The average risk of someone developing colorectal cancer in their lifetime is about 4.5 percent.
The risk once a person has been diagnosed with Crohn's disease is as follows: [36](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:36 "See Footnote 36")
  * After 10 years, 3 percent are likely to have developed colorectal cancer
  * After 20 years, 6 percent are likely to have developed colorectal cancer
  * After 30 years, 8 percent are likely to have developed colorectal cancer


People with Crohn’s disease are advised to attend regular medical checkups in general, which should assist with the early identification and treatment of any associated conditions that arise.
[Read more about colorectal cancer »](https://ada.com/conditions/colorectal-cancer/)
### Pregnancy and fertility
People who are affected by Crohn’s disease can normally follow their usual treatment plan [during pregnancy](https://ada.com/conditions/pregnancy/). Most of the medications and treatment protocols, which are normally prescribed for people with Crohn’s disease, are suitable for pregnant women, with the exception of methotrexate, a type of immunosuppressant medication. 
Regarding the development of the fetus, Crohn’s disease has been associated with the following possible risks: 
  * Low birth weight
  * Preterm delivery
  * Stillbirth
  * Small gestational age


It is strongly recommended that both men and women with Crohn’s disease be in a period of remission at the point of conception.[38](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:38 "See Footnote 38")
## Find out more about your symptoms
## Crohn’s disease FAQs
Q: Does Crohn’s disease reduce one’s life expectancy?  
A:[39](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:39 "See Footnote 39")
Q: How is Crohn’s disease different from ulcerative colitis?  
A:[40](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:40 "See Footnote 40")
The two conditions differ in their symptoms. People with Crohn’s disease may produce stools containing mucus, blood and/or undigested fats, whereas stool samples from people with ulcerative colitis are more likely to contain only mucus and/or blood. Tenesmus (rectal pain) is more characteristic of ulcerative colitis than Crohn’s disease, whereas fistulae and weight loss are more likely to occur in cases of Crohn’s disease. It is common for someone with Crohn’s disease to experience regular fevers, [41](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:41 "See Footnote 41") whereas this would be symptomatic of a severe flare-up in someone with ulcerative colitis. [42](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:42 "See Footnote 42")
Q: Is there a cure for Crohn’s disease?  
A:[43](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/#fn:43 "See Footnote 43")

# COVID-19 and Pneumonia
Written by [Ada’s Medical Knowledge Team](https://ada.com/team/medical/)
Updated on February 10, 2025 at 9:00 AM GMT+2
## On this page
  * [Overview](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-symptoms-and-pneumonia/#overview)

Share this article:
## Overview
  * COVID-19 pneumonia is a complication of an infection with the coronavirus.
  * If you’ve had severe COVID-19 pneumonia, recovery can take up to a year.
  * The possibility of getting COVID-19 pneumonia increases if you have underlying risk factors. 


COVID-19 pneumonia is a respiratory infection
Think you might be experiencing COVID-19 symptoms
## What is COVID-19 pneumonia?
COVID-19 pneumonia is an inflammation of the lungs[COVID-19](https://ada.com/covid/), not everyone infected with the coronavirus develops this condition. Apart from the coronavirus, pneumonia can also be caused by other viruses, bacteria, or even fungi. 
COVID-19 pneumonia usually affects both lungs simultaneously, whereas other types of pneumonia can be limited to one lung or a part of a lung. Pneumonia affects the air sacs
Concerned that you or a loved one may have COVID-19? Start your symptom assessment in the [app](https://ada.com/app/) first.
## What are the common symptoms of COVID-19 pneumonia? 
The symptoms of COVID-19 pneumonia [depend on your risk profile](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-high-risk-groups/) and can be mild to severe. A few groups, in particular, are at risk of falling seriously ill due to pneumonia[1](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-symptoms-and-pneumonia/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1")
  * Babies
  * Older people
  * People with underlying heart or lung conditions such as[ COPD](https://ada.com/covid/copd-and-covid-19/) or [asthma](https://ada.com/conditions/asthma/)
  * Smokers


COVID-19 pneumonia can start suddenly or can develop gradually over a few days. The most commonly reported symptoms [1](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-symptoms-and-pneumonia/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1")
  * A [cough](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-symptom-cough/) combined with yellow or green phlegm 
  * [Shortness of breath](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-shortness-of-breath/)
  * [Fever](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-fever-range/)
  * Chest pain
  * [Body aches](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-symptom-body-aches/)
  * [Feeling tired without a specific cause](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-symptom-fatigue/)
  * [Loss of appetite](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-loss-of-appetite/)
  * Wheezing 
  * Feeling confused or disoriented 


Increased difficulty with breathing is often one of the first symptoms of COVID-19, turning into COVID-19 pneumonia. 
## The risks of COVID-19 pneumonia
COVID-19 pneumonia is a serious condition that often requires hospitalization and may be a cause of death in some cases. It’s essential to monitor your symptoms[1](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-symptoms-and-pneumonia/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1")
  * You’ve had a cough for more than 3 weeks
  * You’re coughing up blood
  * You’re experiencing chest pain that comes and goes or chest pain when breathing or coughing
  * You’re feeling short of breath
  * You’re struggling to breathe and speak 
  * You have pale blue skin 
  * You suddenly feel confused or disoriented


## How is COVID-19 pneumonia diagnosed?
For your physician to diagnose you with COVID-19 pneumonia, you'll first be asked questions about the course of your disease, symptoms, and medical history. Your physician will also perform a physical exam, listen to your lungs, and order diagnostic tests such as chest X-rays or CT scan. 
IA PCR test or blood work can be done for your health provider to track the cause of your pneumonia[2](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-symptoms-and-pneumonia/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2") [3](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-symptoms-and-pneumonia/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3")
## How long does COVID-19 pneumonia last?
COVID-19 pneumonia develops slower and lasts longer than other forms of pneumonia. [the coronavirus can travel easily to different areas in the lungs](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-lungs-symptoms/), causing inflammation in various locations at the same time. This extends the course of the disease and the recovery period. [4](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-symptoms-and-pneumonia/#fn:4 "See Footnote 4")
Most people with COVID-19 pneumonia start feeling better within 3 to 6 weeks. However, people with more severe cases can battle pneumonia for months. It can even take a year with continuous treatment for lung function to return to the levels before the infection with the coronavirus. Getting immediate medical treatment allows for a quicker recovery and increases the survival rate of COVID-19 pneumonia. [4](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-symptoms-and-pneumonia/#fn:4 "See Footnote 4")
## How to treat COVID-19 pneumonia
Treatment for COVID-19 pneumonia [can include the admission of antiviral therapy](https://ada.com/covid/antiviral-medication/) to support the immune system in fighting the virus. Your healthcare provider can give you a prescription to get this medication after assessing your risk of severe illness. 
Less severe cases of COVID-19 pneumonia will be treated at home with a focus on the symptoms. This may include over-the-counter medication to lower the fever and to help against the cough. Drinking sufficient fluids and getting rest is also recommended until the symptoms fade.
In more severe cases, treatment at a hospital can become necessary. 
Corticoids like dexamethasone are not recommended
The CDC also advises against
If there's a bacterial infection present in addition to your infection with the coronavirus, antibiotics [5](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-symptoms-and-pneumonia/#fn:5 "See Footnote 5")
As COVID-19 pneumonia affects your oxygen intake, there’s often a need to administer additional oxygen[6](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-symptoms-and-pneumonia/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6")
## How to prevent COVID-19 pneumonia
Besides the existing therapy for COVID-19-related pneumonia, there are a few things that you can do to prevent the risk of this complication
  * Getting vaccinated and keeping your vaccination up to date
  * Stop smoking 
  * Maintaining good hand hygiene 
  * Keep underlying health issues properly managed


## Wrapping up
COVID-19 pneumonia is a severe complication of COVID-19, which could result in hospitalization and an increased chance of death because of the infection. It's crucial to monitor your symptoms closely if you've been infected with the coronavirus and seek medical attention if your condition worsens. This is especially true if you have underlying risk factors for severe illness due to COVID-19.

## Información general
  * COVID-19 es una enfermedad infecciosa con muchas variantes 
  * Actualmente, Omicron es la variante de COVID-19 más presente en todo el mundo
  * Los síntomas de COVID-19 pueden variar, de una ausencia de síntomas o síntomas leves que se asemejan a un resfriado, hasta síntomas graves que pueden llevar a la hospitalización y la muerte
  * Se puede tratar la mayoría de los casos de COVID-19 en casa. Algunas personas pueden ser elegibles para recibir terapia antivírica


Aprende más acerca de tus síntomas
La guía COVID-19 de [Ada](https://ada.com/app/): todo sobre el coronavirus, variantes, síntomas y tratamientos. Una explicación completa y confiable en un solo lugar, hemos creado una guía completa sobre COVID-19síntomas, diagnóstico, tratamientos 
## ¿Qué es el COVID-19?
El COVID-19 es una enfermedad infecciosa que tiene su origen en 2019 en Wuhan, China. Desde entonces, el coronavirus se ha propagado por todo el mundo y ha mutado muchas veces, [dando lugar a diferentes variantes](https://ada.com/es/covid/nueva-variante-covid-19/)[Omicron](https://ada.com/es/covid/omicron-sintomas/). Esta última es la que predomina actualmente en todo el mundo. 
El coronavirus se propaga a través de diminutas gotitas y partículas de aerosol procedentes de la boca o la nariz de una persona infectada al toser, estornudar, hablar, cantar o respirar. La mayoría de las personas infectadas presentan síntomas leves o moderados. Sin embargo, en algunas personas, el coronavirus puede causar una enfermedad grave, que puede provocar la hospitalización o incluso la muerte. [1](https://ada.com/es/covid/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1")
¿Te preocupa que tú o alguien cercano a ti puedan tener COVID-19? Comienza tu evaluación de síntomas en la app.
## ¿Cuáles son los síntomas del COVID-19?
[El COVID-19 puede causar diversos síntomas](https://ada.com/es/covid/sintomas-covid-19/), con ligeras diferencias según la variante con la que se haya infectado. En general, el coronavirus puede causar: [2](https://ada.com/es/covid/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2") [3](https://ada.com/es/covid/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3")
  * Fiebre o escalofríos
  * [Tos](https://ada.com/es/covid/tos-covid-19/)
  * Dificultad para respirar o dificultad para respirar
  * Fatiga
  * Dolor de cuerpo
  * [Dolor de cabeza](https://ada.com/es/covid/dolor-de-cabeza-covid/)
  * [Pérdida del gusto o del olfato](https://ada.com/es/covid/perdida-olfato-y-gusto-covid-19/)
  * [Dolor de garganta](https://ada.com/es/covid/dolor-de-garganta-covid-19/)
  * Congestión o secreción nasal
  * Pérdida de apetito
  * Náuseas o vómitos
  * Diarrea
  * Erupción cutánea
  * Problemas de memoria y concentración


Los primeros signos de detección del coronavirus
Algunas personas pueden presentar síntomas graves [2](https://ada.com/es/covid/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2")
  * Dificultad para respirar
  * Dolor persistente presión en el pecho
  * Confusión
  * Incapacidad mantenerse despierto
  * Piel pálida, gris  azulada


## ¿Cómo se puede diagnosticar el COVID-19?
Se puede comprobar si estás infectado con el coronavirus mediante una prueba PCRprueba de antígenos[4](https://ada.com/es/covid/#fn:4 "See Footnote 4")
  * Su sensibilidad
  * El precio
  * Las pruebas de antígenos negativas no descartan por completo una infección del coronavirus. Sólo deben utilizarse como resultados preliminares y deben confirmarse mediante una prueba PCR. 
  * Las pruebas PCR pueden indicar un resultado falso positivo para las personas que se hayan infectado con COVID-19 en los últimos 90 días, ya que el ARN viral puede permanecer en el cuerpo.


## ¿Cuánto tiempo dura el COVID-19 en el cuerpo?
Los síntomas de COVID-19 suelen aparecer entre 2 y 14 días después de la exposición al virus. periodo de incubación del COVID-19[generalmente durarán de unos días a unas semanas](https://ada.com/es/covid/cuantos-dias-dura-el-covid/). Sin embargo, algunas personas siguen sufriendo de los síntomas de COVID-19 mucho tiempo después de haberse infectado. Esta situación se llama COVID de larga duración y puede caracterizarse por alguno de los siguientes síntomas: [5](https://ada.com/es/covid/#fn:5 "See Footnote 5") [6](https://ada.com/es/covid/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6")
  * Cansancio extremo
  * Dificultad para respirar o dificultad para respirar
  * Dolor torácico
  * Problemas de memoria y concentración
  * Dificultad para dormir
  * Palpitaciones
  * Mareos o aturdimiento
  * Depresión y ansiedad
  * Sentirse enfermo
  * Cambios en el olfato o el gusto
  * Erupciones cutáneas
  * Tos persistente
  * Dolores de cabeza
  * Dolores de oído o tinnitus
  * Diarrea o dolor de estómago
  * Cambios en el ciclo menstrual


Si crees que estás sufriendo COVID de larga duración, es aconsejable que realices una consulta médica para informarte sobre las posibles opciones de tratamiento.
## ¿Cómo tratar el COVID-19 sin ir al hospital? 
El tratamiento del COVID-19 depende de sus síntomas. Aunque la mayoría de casos de COVID-19 se pueden tratar en casa, algunas personas cumplen los requisitos para recibir terapia antiviral o anticuerpos monoclonales. Que una persona pueda o no recibir este tipo de tratamiento depende de su riesgo de enfermarse gravemente. Los siguientes factores de riesgo afectan el nivel de gravedad que puede provocar el coronavirus: [7](https://ada.com/es/covid/#fn:7 "See Footnote 7") [8](https://ada.com/es/covid/#fn:8 "See Footnote 8") [10](https://ada.com/es/covid/#fn:10 "See Footnote 10") [11](https://ada.com/es/covid/#fn:11 "See Footnote 11")
  * No estar vacunado
  * Tu edad, especialmente si tienes más de 70 años
  * Ciertos tratamientos médicos, como la quimioterapia y la terapia inmunosupresora
  * Enfermedades y afecciones particulares, como enfermedades cardiovasculares e inmunodeficiencias
  * Fumar
  * Hipertensión arterial
  * Obesidad
  * Embarazo
  * Afecciones pulmonares crónicas, como EPOC y asma


Si tienes COVID-19, debes vigilar de cerca tus síntomas para estar preparado para actuar si empeoran. Debes ponerte en contacto con la consulta médica si: [12](https://ada.com/es/covid/#fn:12 "See Footnote 12")
  * Te sientes gradualmente peor
  * Tienes dificultad para respirar sin hacer ejercicio
  * Te sientes muy débil y las tareas básicas se están volviendo demasiado difíciles
  * Tienes temblores o escalofríos
  * Sigues sintiéndote mal después de un mes


Para reducir la posibilidad de enfermarse gravemente por el coronavirus, se recomienda vacunarse y recibir todos los refuerzos recomendados.
## ¿Cuál es la mejor prevención contra el COVID-19?
La prevención contra el COVID-19 es importante, ya que el coronavirus se puede transmitir fácilmente[13](https://ada.com/es/covid/#fn:13 "See Footnote 13")
  * Vacunarte y mantener al día tu vacunación con las dosis de refuerzo recomendadas
  * Lavarte las manos frecuentemente y a fondo con agua y jabón
  * Mejorar la ventilación de los espacios interiores
  * Evitar el contacto con personas que presenten síntomas de COVID-19 o que hayan obtenido resultados afirmativos de la prueba de COVID-19.
  * Utiliza una mascarilla que se ajuste bien y que cubra tanto la nariz como la boca. Las mascarillas pueden establecer una barrera para las partículas que respiras, toses o estornudas. Las mascarillas N95 proporcionan una mayor protección, ya que se ajustan bien a la cara y filtran una gran variedad de partículas, incluyendo al coronavirus.
  * Mantener una distancia de seguridad con los demás


## ¿Cuántos días de cuarentena por COVID-19 son necesarios? 
Mantenerte alejado de los demás es vital para luchar contra la propagación del coronavirus. Si tienes síntomas de COVID-19, debes hacerte una prueba lo antes posible y aislarte 
Si la prueba da positivo, debes permanecer en cuarentena durante al menos 5 días.
El periodo de cuarentena se empieza a contar a partir del día siguiente al primer día en que se presentan los síntomas.[14](https://ada.com/es/covid/#fn:14 "See Footnote 14")
## En resumen
El COVID-19 ha causado gran preocupación durante los últimos años debido a su facilidad de transmisión y al hecho de que el COVID-19 podía provocar una enfermedad repentina y grave en grupos vulnerables. Gracias a los programas de vacunación, a un mejor conocimiento del virus y a los métodos de tratamiento disponibles, el pronóstico general de una infección por el coronavirus ha mejorado drásticamente. No obstante, sigue siendo aconsejable tener precaución y mantener una distancia de seguridad con los demás.

# Coronavirus-Variante Omikron: Inkubationszeit und Symptome
Verfasst von [Adas medizinischem Fachpersonal](https://ada.com/de/team/medical/)
Aktualisiert am 20. Juni 2025 um 11:00 OESZ
## Auf dieser Seite

## Überblick
Omikron ist die derzeit vorherrschende Coronavirus-Variante. Die von Omikron verursachten Symptome [die Inkubationszeit](https://ada.com/de/covid/inkubationszeit-corona/), also die Zeit, die zwischen Infektion und dem Auftreten erster Symptome vergeht, der Coronavirus-Variante Omikron und welche Symptome sie verursachen kann. Außerdem liest Du, wie Infektionen mit Omikron diagnostiziert werden und welche Behandlungsmöglichkeiten es in diesen Fällen gibt.
  * Der erste gemeldete Fall einer Infektion mit der Coronavirus-Variante Omikron wurde im November 2021 in Südafrika bestätigt.
  * Omikron ist derzeit die weltweit vorherrschende Coronavirus-Variante und wird von den Gesundheitsbehörden aufmerksam überwacht.
  * Omikron verursacht hauptsächlich Symptome in den oberen Atemwegen.
  * Diese Coronavirus-Variante ist leicht übertragbar. Deshalb ist es ratsam, sich vor einer Ansteckung zu schützen.


Finde mehr über Deine Symptome heraus.
## Was ist die Coronavirus-Variante Omikron?
Bei der Omikron-Variante handelt es sich um eine Mutation (dauerhafte Veränderung des Erbguts) des ursprünglichen Coronavirus, die Ende 2021 erstmals entdeckt wurde. Derzeit ist Omikron die weltweit am stärksten verbreitete Coronavirus-Variante[1](https://ada.com/de/covid/coronavirus-variante-omikron/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1")
Die aktuell verfügbaren COVID-19-Impfstoffe können auch vor Infektionen mit der Coronavirus-Variante Omikron XBB.1.5 schützen. Die Impfung bietet Schutz vor schweren Erkrankungsverläufen und Todesfällen.
Wenn Du Dir unsicher bist, ob diese Beschwerden auf Dich zutreffen, starte eine 
Wenn Du Dir unsicher bist, ob diese Beschwerden auf Dich zutreffen, starte eine [Symptomanalyse](https://ada.com/de/symptom-assessment-de/?mtm_source=web_articles&mtm_medium=organic&mtm_campaign=;geo:de;lan:ger;cli:ada;prdcat:hejo_match;prd:ada;campff:coronavirus_variante_omikron&mtm_content=;contff:covid).
## Wie sehen die Symptome der Omikron-Variante aus?
Die von Omikron verursachten Symptome sind meistens weniger schwerwiegend im Vergleich zu jenen anderer Varianten wie Delta. Trotzdem kann auch eine Infektion mit der Coronavirus-Variante Omikron zu einem schweren Verlauf mit Krankenhausaufenthalten bis hin zum Tod führen. Daher ist es wichtig, vorsichtig zu bleiben und sich vor einer Infektion zu schützen.[2](https://ada.com/de/covid/coronavirus-variante-omikron/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2")
Im Allgemeinen machen sich die Symptome einer Infektion mit Omikron eher in den oberen Atemwegen 
Zu den weiteren Symptomen der Coronavirus-Variante Omikron gehören unter anderem: [3](https://ada.com/de/covid/coronavirus-variante-omikron/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3")
  * [Halsschmerzen](https://ada.com/de/covid/halsschmerzen-corona/)
  * Laufende Nase
  * Neu auftretender, anhaltender [Husten](https://ada.com/de/covid/corona-husten/)
  * [Hohes Fieber](https://ada.com/de/covid/corona-fieber/)
  * [Muskel- und Gliederschmerzen](https://ada.com/de/covid/muskelschmerzen-corona/)
  * Müdigkeit (Fatigue) ohne ersichtlichen Grund
  * [Kopfschmerzen](https://ada.com/de/covid/corona-kopfschmerzen/)


Bei ErwachsenenKindern.
  * Alter
  * Impfstatus
  * bestehende Grunderkrankungen.


## Wie lange dauern die Symptome bei einer Infektion mit Omikron?
Die Coronavirus-Variante Omikron3 Tagen eine kürzere Inkubationszeit als andere Varianten[4](https://ada.com/de/covid/coronavirus-variante-omikron/#fn:4 "See Footnote 4") Das heißt, die ersten Omikron-Symptome können 3 Tage nach der Infektion auftreten und können Tage bis Wochen bestehen bleiben
Bei manchen Menschen mit [Long-COVID](https://ada.com/de/covid/long-covid-symptome/) können die Symptome auch länger anhalten – zum Beispiel über Wochen und Monate. Wenn Du von Long-COVID betroffen bist, lässt Du Dich am besten hausärztlich beraten.
## Wie kann die Coronavirus-Variante Omikron diagnostiziert werden?
In der Regel wird die Omikron-Variante mithilfe eines PCR-Tests diagnostiziert. Er weist das Erbgut des Coronavirus im Nasen- oder Rachenabstrich nach. Antigen-Schnelltests können auch verwendet werden, sind jedoch weniger empfindlich als PCR-Tests.
[Wenn Du auf eine mögliche Infektion mit dem Coronavirus getestet wirst](https://ada.com/de/covid/), lässt sich die genaue Variante mithilfe einer Gensequenzierung bestimmen. Dabei wird das Erbgut des Coronavirus auf bestimmte Mutationen untersucht, die nur bei der Omikron-Variante auftreten. Die Gensequenzierung wird allerdings eingesetzt, um Informationen über die Verbreitung der Coronavirus-Varianten zu sammeln. Dein Testergebnis enthält in der Regel keine Angaben zur Variante, mit der Du Dich infiziert hast.[5](https://ada.com/de/covid/coronavirus-variante-omikron/#fn:5 "See Footnote 5")
Wenn Du Dir unsicher bist, ob diese Beschwerden auf Dich zutreffen, starte eine 
## Wie lassen sich die Symptome einer Infektion mit der Omikron-Variante behandeln?
Die Behandlung der Omikron-Symptome[6](https://ada.com/de/covid/coronavirus-variante-omikron/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6") [7](https://ada.com/de/covid/coronavirus-variante-omikron/#fn:7 "See Footnote 7")
  * Gründlich ausruhen
  * Ausreichend trinken, vor allem wenn Du Fieber hast
  * Bei Husten ist es besser zu sitzen, als zu liegen
  * Rezeptfreie Schmerzmittel und hustenstillende Medikamente einnehmen


Wenn sich Deine Symptome mit der Zeit verschlimmern oder wenn Du Fragen zu Medikamenten hast, solltest Du Dich unbedingt ärztlich behandeln lassen.
## Das Wichtigste auf einen Blick
Die derzeit vorherrschende Omikron-Variante verursacht ähnliche Symptome wie die anderen Coronavirus-Varianten. Ein Unterschied ist jedoch, dass die unteren Atemwege (wie die Lunge) bei einer Infektion mit der Omikron-Variante meistens weniger betroffen sind

# Aspiração de corpo estranho
Escrito pelo nosso [Medical Knowledge Team](https://ada.com/pt/team/medical/)
Atualizado em 2 de fevereiro de 2022 às 10:16 GMT+2
## Nesta página
  * [Visão geral](https://ada.com/pt/conditions/foreign-body-aspiration/#visao-geral)
  * [Riscos](https://ada.com/pt/conditions/foreign-body-aspiration/#riscos)
  * [Sintomas](https://ada.com/pt/conditions/foreign-body-aspiration/#sintomas)
  * [Diagnóstico](https://ada.com/pt/conditions/foreign-body-aspiration/#diagnostico)
  * [Tratamento](https://ada.com/pt/conditions/foreign-body-aspiration/#tratamento)
  * [Prevenção](https://ada.com/pt/conditions/foreign-body-aspiration/#prevencao)
  * [Prognóstico](https://ada.com/pt/conditions/foreign-body-aspiration/#prognostico)


* * *
Compartilhe esse artigo:
## Visão geral
A aspiração de corpo estranho ocorre quando se engole um objeto não comestível e ele fica preso na garganta ou nas vias respiratórias. Pode ser uma emergência médica, dependendo da gravidade do bloqueio. Lactentes e crianças pequenas tendem a inalar pequenos objetos como botões e bolas de gude, enquanto os adultos em geral inalam itens relativos a alimentos. Os sintomas típicos são tosse, chiado e dificuldade em respirar. O tratamento envolve a gestão da capacidade da pessoa de respirar e a remoção do objeto.
## Riscos
A inalação de pequenos objetos, como moedas e botões, costuma ocorrer com crianças e bebês. Adultos em geral inalam acidentalmente itens relativos à alimentação, tais como ossos, palitos, ou pedaços de frutas. Adultos com algumas doenças neurológicas, tais como demência, tem maior risco de inalar objetos estranhos.
## Sintomas
Os sintomas dependem do objeto inalado, onde se aloja nas vias aéreas e o tempo decorrido desde que o objeto foi inalado. Os sintomas típicos incluem respiração ofegante, asfixia, dificuldade em respirar, coloração azulada da face e uma tosse persistente. Se o objeto estiver causando um bloqueio importante nas vias aéreas, estes sintomas ocorrem de repente e requerem tratamento imediato em um departamento de emergência. Se o objeto ficou nas vias aéreas durante algum tempo, causou uma infecção pulmonar, pode haver febre, um pulso rápido, e, possivelmente, desmaio.
## Diagnóstico
O diagnóstico é feito por um médico que avalia os sintomas e faz um exame físico. Muitas vezes, é necessário um raio-X, TC (tomografia computadorizada) do peito ou uma broncoscopia (usando uma câmera para olhar as vias respiratórias) para confirmar o diagnóstico.
## Tratamento
O tratamento envolve tratar da capacidade da pessoa respirar e remover o corpo estranho. Se a pessoa não consegue respirar, é muito importante o auxílio à respiração e remoção urgentes. Um primeiro passo para remover o objeto é tentar induzir a pessoa a tossir. Se isso não funcionar, intervenção médica será necessária, seja por broncoscopia (uma câmera introduzida para examinar as vias respiratórias) ou, como último recurso, por cirurgia. Se houver uma infecção, antibióticos podem ser administrados.
## Prevenção
Manter pequenos objetos como moedas, botões, pilhas, longe das crianças, ensinar-lhes a mastigar bem e aconselhá-los a não falar ou brincar enquanto comem pode evitar a ingestão de corpo estranho em crianças pequenas.
## Prognóstico
Quase todos os corpos estranhos podem ser removidos das vias aéreas com um broncoscópio. Se o objeto não causar problemas respiratórios de emergência e for removido imediatamente, a maioria das pessoas se recupera bem. A inalação de objetos grandes pode ser fatal. As complicações ocorrem mais frequentemente quando o diagnóstico é feito 24 horas após a inalação.

# COVID-19 (Coronavirus-Krankheit 2019)
Verfasst von [Adas medizinischem Fachpersonal](https://ada.com/de/team/medical/)
Aktualisiert am 20. Januar 2025 um 15:00 OEZ
## Auf dieser Seite
  * [COVID-19](https://ada.com/de/conditions/covid-19/#covid-19)
  * [Häufige Symptome von COVID-19](https://ada.com/de/conditions/covid-19/#haeufige-symptome-von-covid-19)
  * [Inkubationszeit und Ansteckung](https://ada.com/de/conditions/covid-19/#inkubationszeit-und-ansteckung)
  * [Diagnose von COVID-19](https://ada.com/de/conditions/covid-19/#diagnose-von-covid-19)
  * [Behandlung von COVID-19](https://ada.com/de/conditions/covid-19/#behandlung-von-covid-19)
    * [Vorbeugung von COVID-19](https://ada.com/de/conditions/covid-19/#vorbeugung-von-covid-19)
  * [FAQ](https://ada.com/de/conditions/covid-19/#faq)


* * *
Artikel teilen:
Die Coronavirus-Erkrankung 2019 (coronavirus disease 2019, COVID-19) wird durch eine Infektion mit dem Coronavirus SARS-CoV-2 verursacht. Es wurde erstmals Anfang Dezember 2019 in der chinesischen Stadt Wuhan nachgewiesen. [1](https://ada.com/de/conditions/covid-19/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") Die Bezeichnung des Virus als „SARS-CoV-2“ hat die Weltgesundheitsorganisation (WHO) vorgeschlagen. [2](https://ada.com/de/conditions/covid-19/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2")
Finde mehr über Deine Symptome heraus.
## Die Ursache von COVID-19
Der COVID-19-Erreger SARS-CoV-2 gehört zur großen Familie der Coronaviren, die sowohl Menschen als auch Tiere infizieren können. Coronaviren können von Mensch zu Mensch, aber auch zwischen manchen Tierarten und Menschen übertragen werden. In der Vergangenheit hat diese Tier-Mensch-Übertragung von Coronaviren zu größeren Krankheitsausbrüchen geführt, zum Beispiel [3](https://ada.com/de/conditions/covid-19/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3")
  * Middle East Respiratory Syndrome-Coronavirus (MERS-CoV) zwischen Kamelen und Menschen
  * Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome-Coronavirus (SARS-CoV) von Zibetkatzen und Fledermäusen auf den Menschen


Auch bei SARS-CoV-2 vermutet man, dass es von Tieren stammt. Denn vor dem Ausbruch der Corona-Pandemie Ende Januar 2020 waren einige Infizierte auf einem chinesischen Markt mit Wildtieren und Geflügel in Kontakt gekommen. Im Verdacht stehen vor allem Fledermäuse, was jedoch noch nicht abschließend bestätigt ist. Möglicherweise gab es noch andere Zwischenüberträger wie das Malaiische Schuppentier (Pangolin). [3](https://ada.com/de/conditions/covid-19/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3")
Heute weiß man, dass das Coronavirus SARS-CoV-2 – wie andere Atemwegserreger – über winzige Tröpfchen von Mensch zu Mensch übertragen werden. Diese Flüssigkeitspartikel entstehen zum Beispiel beim Sprechen, Niesen oder Husten. Wenn Du die virushaltigen kleinen Tröpfchen über Mund und Nase einatmest, kannst Du Dich mit dem Coronavirus anstecken und an COVID-19 erkranken. [1](https://ada.com/de/conditions/covid-19/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [4](https://ada.com/de/conditions/covid-19/#fn:4 "See Footnote 4")
Mit der [Ada-App](https://ada.com/de/app/) kannst Du Deine Symptome ganz einfach checken. 
## Häufige Symptome von COVID-19
[Typische Anzeichen von COVID-19](https://ada.com/de/covid/corona-symptome/) sind erkältungsähnliche Beschwerden, wie zum Beispiel:
  * [Husten](https://ada.com/de/covid/corona-husten/)
  * [Fieber](https://ada.com/de/covid/corona-fieber/)
  * Schnupfen
  * Müdigkeit
  * [Kopfschmerzen](https://ada.com/de/covid/corona-kopfschmerzen/)
  * [Halsschmerzen](https://ada.com/de/covid/halsschmerzen-corona/)
  * [Gliederschmerzen](https://ada.com/de/covid/gliederschmerzen-corona/)


Weitere mögliche COVID-19-Symptome sind unter anderem:
  * [Geruchs- und/oder Geschmacksverlust](https://ada.com/de/covid/geruchs-und-geschmacksverlust-corona/)
  * Magen-/Darmsymptome wie [Übelkeit, Erbrechen](https://ada.com/de/covid/corona-uebelkeit-und-erbrechen/) und [Durchfall](https://ada.com/de/covid/corona-durchfall/)
  * Kurzatmigkeit bis hin zu Atemnot


Außerdem kann COVID-19 das Herz-Kreislauf- und Nerven-System sowie die Haut und weitere Organsysteme betreffen. Wichtig zu wissen
Die meisten erleben einen milden bis mittelschweren Verlauf der COVID-19-Symptome. Bei einigen Menschen mit Risikofaktoren kann es allerdings zu einem schwerwiegenden bis lebensbedrohlichen Verlauf mit Lungenentzündung, Multiorganversagen oder Embolien kommen. [1](https://ada.com/de/conditions/covid-19/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1")
Zu diesen Risikofaktoren gehören beispielsweise [1](https://ada.com/de/conditions/covid-19/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [5](https://ada.com/de/conditions/covid-19/#fn:5 "See Footnote 5")
  * ein höheres Alter (ab 60 Jahren)
  * Grunderkrankungen wie Herz-Kreislauf-Erkrankungen, Diabetes und Asthma
  * Krebserkrankungen
  * ein geschwächtes Immunsystem
  * ein starkes Übergewicht (Adipositas)


Bei den meisten Infizierten mit einem milden bis mittelschweren COVID-19-Verlauf bessern sich die Symptome innerhalb von 1 bis 2 Wochen. Manche erkranken jedoch an [Long-COVID](https://ada.com/de/covid/long-covid-symptome/) und haben nach der akuten Coronavirus-Infektion über Wochen oder Monate weiter Beschwerden. [1](https://ada.com/de/conditions/covid-19/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1")
## Inkubationszeit und Ansteckung
Im Durchschnitt verstreichen 5,8 Tage von der Ansteckung mit dem Coronavirus bis zu den ersten COVID-19-Symptomen. Allerdings kann diese [Inkubationszeit bei einigen Menschen](https://ada.com/de/covid/inkubationszeit-corona/) bis zu 12 Tage dauern. Sie hängt zum Beispiel von der Coronavirus-Variante ab. [4](https://ada.com/de/conditions/covid-19/#fn:4 "See Footnote 4")
Es ist bislang unklar, wie lange jemand mit COVID-19 ansteckend bleibt. Man weiß aber, dass die höchste Ansteckungsfähigkeit kurz vor und nach dem Beginn der Symptome und damit Coronaviren meistens übertragen werden, bevor die ersten Symptome auftreten. Als Faustregel gilt, dass Menschen mit einem leichten bis mittelschweren COVID-19-Verlauf etwa 10 Tage nach dem Auftreten der ersten Symptome deutlich weniger ansteckend sind. [4](https://ada.com/de/conditions/covid-19/#fn:4 "See Footnote 4")
Seit dem offiziellen Ende der Corona-Pandemie im Jahr 2023, gibt es keine Regeln mehr, nach denen Du Dich wegen einer Coronavirus-Infektion selbst isolieren und dann „frei-testen“ musst. Es ist aber sinnvoll, dass Du 3 bis 5 Tage zu Hause bleibst, wenn Du Symptome einer Atemwegsinfektion hast. [6](https://ada.com/de/conditions/covid-19/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6") [7](https://ada.com/de/conditions/covid-19/#fn:7 "See Footnote 7")
## Diagnose von COVID-19
COVID-19 lässt sich zweifelsfrei anhand eines Nasen- oder Rachenabstrichs diagnostizieren. Dazu gibt es 2 Testverfahren: [1](https://ada.com/de/conditions/covid-19/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [4](https://ada.com/de/conditions/covid-19/#fn:4 "See Footnote 4")
  * PCR-Tests können das Erbgut des Coronavirus nachweisen.
  * Mit Schnelltests werden bestimmte Coronavirus-Antigene (Eiweißmoleküle) erkannt.


Mit der [Ada-App](https://ada.com/de/app/) kannst Du Deine Symptome ganz einfach checken. 
## Behandlung von COVID-19
[Die COVID-19-Behandlung](https://ada.com/de/covid/corona-medikament-und-behandlung/) orientiert sich am Schweregrad der Symptome und ob Risikofaktoren für einen schweren Verlauf bestehen. [8](https://ada.com/de/conditions/covid-19/#fn:8 "See Footnote 8") Für die Mehrheit mit leichten bis mittelschweren Symptomen reichen Hausmittel aus – zum Beispiel: [9](https://ada.com/de/conditions/covid-19/#fn:9 "See Footnote 9")
  * Viel Ruhe
  * Viel Trinken
  * Bei Bedarf: rezeptfreie fiebersenkende Medikamente einnehmen.


Bei einem Risiko für einen schweren COVID-19-Verlauf können spezielle Medikamente angewendet werden. Dazu gehören antivirale Therapien, die sich gegen das Coronavirus richten, und Medikamente, die das Immunsystem unterstützen. 
### Vorbeugung von COVID-19
Du kannst mit verschiedenen Maßnahmen einer Ansteckung mit dem Coronavirus und damit COVID-19 vorbeugen: [10](https://ada.com/de/conditions/covid-19/#fn:10 "See Footnote 10")
  * Lasse Dich gegen COVID-19 impfen. Die Impfung kann Dich vor einem schweren COVID-19-Verlauf schützen.
  * Während der Erkältungssaison kannst Du einen Mund-Nasen-Schutz tragen – vor allem, wenn Du Dich in überfüllten Räumen aufhältst.
  * Halte die bekannten Hygieneregeln wie regelmäßiges Händewaschen ein.

# Durma melhor
[Ada](https://ada.com/pt/editorial/writers/ada/)
Revisado por médicos
Atualizado em 7 de março de 2025 às 11:00 GMT+2
O sono é um dos grandes mistérios da vida. Em média, passamos um terço das nossas vidas a dormir, mas os cientistas ainda não conseguem estabelecer uma teoria que explique por que é tão essencial para nossas vidas.[1](https://ada.com/pt/editorial/sleeping-better/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") O que sabemos é que desligar durante a noite dá a nossos corpos e mentes tempo para descansar, regenerar e reorganizar.
A maioria dos adultos saudáveis ​​precisa de sete a nove horas de sono todas as noites, ou começarão a se sentir cansados ​​e pouco produtivos durante o dia. A longo prazo, sono insuficiente pode causar problemas de saúde tanto a nivel mental como físico.[2](https://ada.com/pt/editorial/sleeping-better/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2")
O sono é essencial para uma vida saudável e é uma atividade que a maioria de nós adora. Então, por que tantos de nós enfrentam problemas em dormir bem?
Vamos dar uma olhada no que atrapalha uma boa noite de sono e as mudanças que você pode fazer para garantir o descanso de que precisa.
## O que está atrapalhando seu sono?
Prazos para entregar trabalho, social media e os últimos seriados estão constantemente competindo por nossa atenção. Com nosso estilo de vida sempre ativo e cheio de distrações, pode ser difícil fazer com que nossas mentes parem de girar e relaxem à noite. Jogue nesse mix outros fatores como cafeína e álcool e dá para entender por que tantos de nós têm dificuldades em adormecer.
Às vezes, fatores fora de seu controle também podem interromper seu sono. Pode ser um bebê recém-nascido, trabalhando no turno da noite ou problemas de saúde existentes.
Felizmente, ao seguir alguns passos simples de higiene do sono, você pode adormecer com mais facilidade no final do dia e acordar revigorado.
## Como você pode melhorar sua higiene do sono?
Higiene do sono não significa tomar um bom banho antes de dormir (embora possa ajudar). Significa introduzir hábitos que melhorem a qualidade e a quantidade do seu sono.[3](https://ada.com/pt/editorial/sleeping-better/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3") Aqui estão nossas cinco principais dicas para uma melhor higiene do sono.
### 1. Fique ativo durante o dia.
Apenas 30 minutos de exercícios moderados durante o dia deixam seu corpo pronto para uma boa noite de sono. Deixe pelo menos uma hora entre os exercícios e a hora de dormir para dar ao corpo uma chance de se acalmar.
### 2. Crie uma rotina noturna.
Uma rotina noturna ajuda o corpo e a mente a se prepararem para dormir. Tome um banho ou uma ducha, faça uma xícara de chá de ervas e leia um livro (de preferência com páginas de papel). Se puder, comprometa-se com uma hora de dormir que permita sete a nove horas de sono. Tente evitar a tela de celulares ou computadores pelo menos uma hora antes de dormir. Se você ainda se sentir acordado no final do dia, técnicas de respiração ou relaxamento podem ajudar.
### 3. Crie um ambiente de sono relaxante.
Desligue as luzes e certifique-se de que sua cama é confortável e tem travesseiros e cobertores adequados. Seu quarto deve ser fresco, silencioso e escuro - tapa-olhos e fones de ouvido ajudam, se necessário. Mantenha seu telefone em outro quarto e use um despertador para acordá-lo se precisar. Tente limitar o tempo que você passa acordado em seu quarto.
### 4. Limite o consumo de cafeína e álcool.
Evite chás (com cafeína como chá preto), café e outras bebidas cafeinadas após o almoço. Não se esqueça: alguns refrigerantes geralmente contêm altos níveis de cafeína, então verifique o rótulo ou, melhor ainda, beba água. O álcool também pode causar estragos no sono. Você pode adormecer mais facilmente depois de algumas taças de vinho, mas beber álcool pode interromper e reduzir a qualidade do seu sono.
### 5. Saia da cama se não conseguir dormir.
Pode parecer contra-intuitivo, mas se você ficar acordado por mais de 20 minutos, levante-se e faça outra coisa durante 10 minutos. Estique o seu corpo, medite ou leia um livro em outra parte da casa. Escrever os pensamentos que estão girando em sua cabeça também pode ajudar.
No caso de você continuar a ter dificuldades de sono mesmo depois de tentar essas técnicas ou os seus problemas de sono estarem relacionados com problemas respiratórios durante o sono, peça ajuda a um parceiro, ou amigo e entre em contato com seu médico.
Com apenas algumas pequenas mudanças, você pode melhorar seu sono e levar uma vida mais saudável e feliz. Então, apague as luzes, feche os olhos e tenha uma boa noite de sono.
