# COVID-19 Symptom: Costochondritis
Written by [Ada’s Medical Knowledge Team](https://ada.com/team/medical/)
Updated on January 29, 2025 at 2:02 PM GMT+2
## On this page
  * [Overview](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-costochondritis/#overview)
  * [Can COVID-19 cause costochondritis?](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-costochondritis/#can-covid-19-cause-costochondritis)
  * [Duration](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-costochondritis/#duration)
  * [Causes of chest pain](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-costochondritis/#causes-of-chest-pain)
  * [Treatments](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-costochondritis/#treatments)
  * [Wrapping up](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-costochondritis/#wrapping-up)
  * [FAQs](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-costochondritis/#faqs)


* * *
Share this article:
## Overview
  * Costochondritis is an inflammation of the cartilage that connects the ribs to the breastbone.
  * Chest pain and tenderness can be symptoms of costochondritis related to COVID-19.
  * The treatment for costochondritis generally involves pain management and anti-inflammatory medications.
  * Although costochondritis related to COVID-19 does not usually cause permanent problems, it can recur periodically.


Think you might be experiencing COVID-19 symptoms
Costochondritisif you have COVID-19
Because chest pain should be taken seriously, it’s essential to understand this symptom so you can contact your doctor if there's cause for concern.
## Can COVID-19 cause costochondritis?
Costochondritis related to COVID-19 is a benignconsequence of an infection 
[Costochondritis is an inflammation of the middle part of your chest](https://ada.com/conditions/costochondritis/) where your ribs meet your breastbone. This inflammation can cause sharp chest pain,[1](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-costochondritis/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [2](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-costochondritis/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2")
  * Breathing deeply
  * Moving your upper body
  * Touching the middle of your chest


The cause of costochondritis related to COVID-19 isn’t well established. Some studies suggest that it's related to the inflammation caused by the diseasecontinuous coughing[3](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-costochondritis/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3")
Costochondritis can also be caused by other factors[1](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-costochondritis/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1")
  * Chest injury
  * Coughing a lot
  * Viral respiratory infections 
  * Lifting heavy weights
  * [Fibromyalgia](https://ada.com/conditions/fibromyalgia/)
  * [Rheumatoid arthritis](https://ada.com/conditions/rheumatoid-arthritis/)


The coronavirus may cause severe distress to the joints between the cartilage of the ribs and the breastbone due to respiratory infection and continuous coughing. Therefore, some people might experience costochondritis after COVID. [4](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-costochondritis/#fn:4 "See Footnote 4") [5](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-costochondritis/#fn:5 "See Footnote 5")
Concerned that you or a loved one may have COVID-19? Start your symptom assessment in the [app](https://ada.com/app/) first.
## How long does costochondritis with COVID-19 last?
As costochondritis with COVID is [strongly related to coughing](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-symptom-cough/) and viral infection, most cases of the inflammation go away a few weeks to months after the coughing has stopped.[1](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-costochondritis/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1")
## What else can cause chest pain?
Although the chest pain caused by costochondritis may be very sharp and distressing, it’s harmless. However, other conditions must[2](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-costochondritis/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2") [6](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-costochondritis/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6")
  * [Pneumothorax](https://ada.com/conditions/pneumothorax/)
  * [Pneumonia](https://ada.com/conditions/pneumonia/) or other chest infections
  * Acute coronary syndrome
  * [Aortic dissection](https://ada.com/conditions/aortic-dissection/)
  * [Lung embolism](https://ada.com/conditions/pulmonary-embolism/)
  * Perforation of the esophagus 
  * Broken ribs
  * Anxiety or [panic attacks](https://ada.com/conditions/signs-of-panic-attack/)
  * [Shingles](https://ada.com/signs-of-shingles/) - chest pain that can be accompanied by a rash that turns into blisters and a tingling feeling on the skin 
  * Heartburn or indigestion
  * Any injury to the chest


Your doctor should always check chest pain because some conditions that cause chest pain require immediate intervention. You should contact your doctor immediately if[1](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-costochondritis/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1")
  * You experience sudden chest pain that persists for more than 15 minutes
  * The pain spreads to your arms, back, neck, or jaw 
  * The pain makes your chest feel tight or heavy
  * You experience shortness of breath.


## How can costochondritis due to COVID-19 be treated?
Costochondritis is a benign condition that typically goes away on its own
If the pain is uncomfortable, several treatment options[1](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-costochondritis/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [5](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-costochondritis/#fn:5 "See Footnote 5")
  * Painkillers
  * NSAIDs
  * Local anesthetic or steroid injection
  * Rest


By combining pain management strategies with rest, you can effectively manage your costochondritis symptoms and speed up the healing process.
## Wrapping up
Costochondritis may be caused by COVID-19 
## Find out more about your symptoms
## Costochondritis and COVID-19 FAQs
Q: Can you still get costochondritis if you took the COVID vaccine? 
Q: Does COVID give you costochondritis?
Q: Does COVID-19 cause sternum pain?
Q: What does long COVID chest pain feel like?[Long COVID](https://ada.com/covid/covid-19-long-covid/) chest pain can vary in intensity and may be described differently by different individuals. Some people may experience a sharp or stabbing pain in the chest, while others may describe the pain as a dull ache or pressure in the chest. The pain may also be intermittent or constant and may be accompanied by other symptoms such as shortness of breath, fatigue, and palpitations.

# Ugonjwa wa bawasiri
Imeandikwa na [Timu ya Ada ya Maarifa ya Kitiba](https://ada.com/sw/team/medical/)
Imesasishwa tarehe 10 Juni 2024, 15:00 GMT +3
## Katika ukurasa huu
  * [Bawasiri ni nini?](https://ada.com/sw/conditions/hemorrhoids/#bawasiri-ni-nini)
  * [Dalili za Bawasiri](https://ada.com/sw/conditions/hemorrhoids/#dalili-za-bawasiri)
  * [Vihatarishi vya Bawasiri](https://ada.com/sw/conditions/hemorrhoids/#vihatarishi-vya-bawasiri)
  * [Utambuzi wa Bawasiri](https://ada.com/sw/conditions/hemorrhoids/#utambuzi-wa-bawasiri)
  * [Matibabu ya Bawasiri](https://ada.com/sw/conditions/hemorrhoids/#matibabu-ya-bawasiri)
  * [Kinga ya Bawasiri](https://ada.com/sw/conditions/hemorrhoids/#kinga-ya-bawasiri)
  * [Hitimisho](https://ada.com/sw/conditions/hemorrhoids/#hitimisho)

Washirikishe wengine kwenye makala hii:
## Bawasiri ni nini?
Bawasiri ni kuvimba kwa mishipa ya damu iliyopo ndani ya au katika eneo linalozunguka njia ya haja kubwa[1](https://ada.com/sw/conditions/hemorrhoids/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") Madhara ya bawasiri ya ndani ni pamoja na damu kutoka wakati wa kujisaidia, damu kuganda ndani ya mishipa ya damu na maumivu.
Unafikiri unaweza kuwa unapata dalili za bawasiri
Kutokea kwa bawasiri kunaweza kuhusishwa na hali kama uzee, ujauzito, kuharisha au choo kufunga (constipation), saratani kwenye nyonga au kuketi kwa muda mrefu. Tiba ya bawasiri inategemea aina ya bawasiri na ukubwa wa tatizo. Matibabu ya bawasiri yanaweza kuhusisha matumizi ya dawa au upasuaji mdogo.
## Anza sasa kufanya maamuzi mazuri zaidi kuhusu afya
## Dalili za Bawasiri
Inakadiriwa 40% ya watu wenye bawasiri hawana dalili za moja kwa moja.[2](https://ada.com/sw/conditions/hemorrhoids/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2") Dalili za bawasiri hujumuisha maumivu, mwasho na hisia ya kitu kinachokera katika eneo linalozunguka njia ya haja kubwa. Baadhi ya watu hupata shida kujisaidia haja kubwa na hutokwa damu wanapojisaidia. Wakati mwingine mishipa ya damu huweza kujitokeza nje. Ikiwa hali hii inatokea, inawezekana kuhisi uvimbe mdogo katika eneo husika.
_[kikagua dalili](https://ada.com/sw/app/) chetu._
## Vihatarishi vya Bawasiri
Bawasiri hutokea pale shinikizo huongezeka kwenye mishipa ya damu inayozunguka njia ya haja kubwa. Hii huweza kuwa matokeo ya kitu kinachokandamiza utumbo, kama vile wakati wa ujauzito, au huweza kutokea kutokana na kujikamua sana wakati wa haja kubwa kutokana na kufunga choo au kuharisha kwa muda mrefu. Hali hii hutokea sana na hutokea zaidi kadri umri unavyoongezeka. Watu wenye uzito wa kupita kiasi wana uwezekano mkubwa wa kupata bawasiri. Vitu vingine vinavyoongeza hatari ya kupata bawasiri ni pamoja na:
  * Kuwa na uzito wa mwili kupita kiasi, ujauzito, na kula vyakula visivyo na nyuzinyuzi (fibre) za kutosha
  * Kubeba vitu vizito mara kwa mara
  * Kuhara kwa muda mrefu na kufunga choo (constipation)
  * Kujamiiana kinyume na maumbile
  * Historia ya uwepo wa ugonjwa wa bawasiri katika familia
  * Magonjwa yanayoathiri njia ya haja kubwa
  * Kuketi kwa muda mrefu
  * Uzee na matatizo ya kutopata choo. [1](https://ada.com/sw/conditions/hemorrhoids/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1")


## Utambuzi wa Bawasiri
Utambuzi hufanywa na daktari
_[kikagua dalili](https://ada.com/sw/app/) chetu._
## Matibabu ya Bawasiri
Bawasiri inatibika na kuna njia mbalimbali za kutibu bawasiri. Tiba halisi ya bawasiri ni kuhakikisha kupata choo kilaini na kuepuka kufunga choo, ili kuepuka hali kuwa mbaya zaidi. Krimu za kupaka na dawa za kuingiza katika njia ya haja kubwa (suppositories) zinaweza kusaidia kupunguza uvimbe, mwasho na maumivu. Dawa hizi hupatikana katika maduka ya dawa. Kuna matibabu mengine ambapo sindano au kamba maalum hutumika ili kupunguza ukubwa wa mishipa ya damu. Dawa ya bawasiri sugu ni upasuaji.
## Kinga ya Bawasiri
Kuhakikisha unapata choo kilaini husaidia kuzuia bawasiri na kupunguza kujirudia kwa dalili za bawasiri. Hii huwezekana kwa kula vyakula vyenye nyuzinyuzi (fiber),kunywa maji ya kutosha, kuwa na uzito unaofaa, kuepuka kukaa kwa muda mrefu, kuepuka kujikamua wakati wa haja kubwa na kuepuka kubeba vitu vizito mara kwa mara.[3](https://ada.com/sw/conditions/hemorrhoids/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3")
## Hitimisho
Bawasiri ni hali inayoweza kukera lakini mara nyingi hazina madhara mabaya kwa afya ya binadamu. Ugonjwa huu unaweza kuisha wenyewe ndani ya wiki. Bawasiri mara nyingi hujirudia, na hali huzidi kuwa mbaya kadiri muda unavyosonga mbele. Bawasiri ni tatizo la kawaida ambalo linaweza kuathiri watu wengi wakati fulani maishani mwao. Kwa bahati nzuri, kuna hatua ambazo mtu anaweza kuchukua kuboresha hali hii au kuzuia kujirudia. Kwa mfano, kuhakikisha ulaji wa chakula chenye ufumwele (fiber) mwingi na kunywa maji ya kutosha kunaweza kusaidia kuzuia tatizo la bawasiri.
Ili kupunguza dalili za bawasiri, unaweza kujaribu matibabu ya nyumbani kama vile kujikanda kwa barafu ili kupunguza uvimbe au kutumia dawa za kupunguza maumivu. Hata hivyo, ni muhimu kushauriana na daktari ikiwa dalili zinazidi kuwa mbaya au nafuu haijapatiakana baada ya muda mfupi ili kupata ushauri na matibabu sahihi.
## Anza sasa kufanya maamuzi mazuri zaidi kuhusu afya
## Maswali Yanayoulizwa Mara kwa Mara (FAQs)
S: Je, ni yapi madhara ya bawasiri kwa mwanamke?  
J: Madhara ya bawasiri kwa mwanamke yanaweza kuwa ya kukera na kuharibu ustawi wake wa kila siku. Wanawake wanaweza kukabiliwa na maumivu makali, kuvuja damu wakati wa kujisaidia haja kubwa, na hata kuhisi aibu au unyonge kwa sababu ya hali hii. Bawasiri inaweza kuathiri pia shughuli za kazi na kuleta changamoto za kijamii na kiakili. Ni muhimu kwa wanawake wanaokabiliwa na bawasiri kutafuta ushauri wa matibabu ili kupata suluhisho sahihi na kuboresha hali yao ya afya na ustawi.
S: Je, bawasiri husababishwa na nini?  
J: Bawasiri hutokana na sababu mbalimbali, ikiwa ni pamoja na matatizo ya choo kigumu au kuhara, shinikizo la ziada tumboni wakati wa ujauzito, kuketi kwa muda mrefu, kuwa na uzito kupita kiasi, na mabadiliko ya homoni wakati wa ujauzito. Matatizo haya husababisha kuziba kwa mishipa ya damu kwenye njia ya haja kubwa, na hivyo kusababisha bawasiri. Kudumisha mtindo wa maisha wenye manufaa kiafya ni muhimu katika kuzuia tatizo hili au kupunguza hatari ya kukabiliwa nalo.
S: Je, dawa ya bawasiri sugu ni ipi?  
J: Dawa ya bawasiri sugu inaweza kutofautiana kulingana na hali ya mtu binafsi na ukali wa bawasiri husika. Katika matukio ya bawasiri sugu, mtaalamu wa afya anaweza kupendekeza matibabu mbalimbali kama vile matumizi ya mafuta au vidonge vya kupunguza maumivu, dawa za kupaka ili kupunguza uvimbe, na mabadiliko ya mtindo wa maisha kama vile lishe bora yenye ufumwele mwingi na kunywa maji ya kutosha. Katika hali mbaya zaidi, upasuaji unaweza kuhitajika kutibu bawasiri sugu. Hivyo basi, ni muhimu kushauriana na mtaalamu wa afya ili kupata matibabu sahihi.

Artikel teilen:
## Was ist Fibromyalgie?
Fibromyalgie ist ein chronisches Schmerzsyndrom, das sich durch weit verbreitete Muskelschmerzen und Druckempfindlichkeit äußert. Die betroffenen Stellen wechseln typischerweise zwischen den Muskeln, Gelenken und dem Rücken.
Weitere Symptome sind Bauchschmerzen, Kopfschmerzen, ein allgemeines Unwohlsein, Morgensteifigkeit und ein schlechter Schlaf. Es wurde noch keine eindeutige Ursache für die Fibromyalgie gefunden, sie weist jedoch eine starke Tendenz auf, familiär gehäuft vorzukommen. Sie tritt eher bei Frauen im Alter von 20 bis 50 Jahren auf.
Die Diagnose einer Fibromyalgie [1](https://ada.com/de/conditions/fibromyalgia/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") basiert auf dem Muster und der Dauer der Symptome, wobei andere mögliche Ursachen für die Symptome ausgeschlossen werden. Training, Schmerzmittel und emotionale Unterstützung bilden die Grundlage einer Behandlung. Es gibt keine spezifische Heilung für die Fibromyalgie. Einige Betroffene lernen, mit ihren Symptomen umzugehen, und andere haben wiederum Schmerzen, die nicht gut auf eine Behandlung ansprechen.
Hast du möglicherweise Fibromyalgie? 
## Was ist die Ursache von Fibromyalgie?
Die Ursachen für die Fibromyalgie sind größtenteils unbekannt.
Hierzu gehören:
  * Fälle von Fibromyalgie in der Familie,
  * [Depression](https://ada.com/de/conditions/depressive-episode/),
  * Schlafstörungen,
  * Stress
  * und das Erleiden einer Muskelverletzung
  * oder eines emotionalen Traumas.


Diese Erkrankung tritt am häufigsten bei Frauen im Alter zwischen 20 und 50 Jahren auf.
## Welche Symptome hat man bei Fibromyalgie?
Das Hauptsymptom der Fibromyalgie ist ein tiefer, brennender Schmerz, der in den Muskeln auf beiden Körperseiten und an verschiedenen Stellen auftritt.
Weitere Symptome
  * eine ungewöhnliche Müdigkeit,
  * Schlafschwierigkeiten,
  * Konzentrationsschwierigkeiten und
  * Gedächtnisprobleme.


## Wie wird Fibromyalgie diagnostiziert?
Die Diagnose kann auf Grundlage der Symptome, der Dauer der Schmerzen und einer körperlichen Untersuchung erfolgen.Symptom-Tagebuch
Zur Bestätigung der Diagnose sollten jedoch andere mögliche Ursachen für die Symptome von einem Arzt ausgeschlossen werden. Blut- und Urintests werden häufig durchgeführt, um andere Erkrankungen auszuschließen.
## Wie wird Fibromyalgie behandelt?
Die Behandlung der Fibromyalgie kann sich als schwierig erweisen, da die Ursache nicht hinreichend bekannt ist.
Sollten diese Methoden keine Wirkung zeigen, so sollte ein Schmerzspezialist aufgesucht werden, der möglicherweise andere Medikamente empfehlen kann. Für viele von Fibromyalgie betroffene Personen sind Selbsthilfegruppen oder eine Beratung hilfreich, um mit der Diagnose zurechtzukommen und mit den Langzeitschmerzen umzugehen.
## Wie ist die Prognose bei Fibromyalgie?
Fibromyalgie ist häufig eine längerfristige Erkrankung, für die es keine spezifische Heilung gibt. Einige Betroffene lernen, mit ihren Symptomen umzugehen, und andere wiederum haben fortbestehende Schmerzen. In diesen Fällen sind eine Beratung und emotionale Unterstützung sehr wichtig.
## Finde mehr über Deine Symptome heraus

# Hodenkrebs
Verfasst von [Adas medizinischem Fachpersonal](https://ada.com/de/team/medical/)
Aktualisiert am 15. Februar 2022 um 10:00 OEZ
## Auf dieser Seite
  * [Was ist Hodenkrebs?](https://ada.com/de/conditions/testicular-cancer/#was-ist-hodenkrebs)
  * [Risiken](https://ada.com/de/conditions/testicular-cancer/#risiken)
  * [Symptome](https://ada.com/de/conditions/testicular-cancer/#symptome)
  * [Diagnose](https://ada.com/de/conditions/testicular-cancer/#diagnose)
  * [Behandlung](https://ada.com/de/conditions/testicular-cancer/#behandlung)
  * [Prognose](https://ada.com/de/conditions/testicular-cancer/#prognose)
  * [Vorsorge](https://ada.com/de/conditions/testicular-cancer/#vorsorge)


* * *
Artikel teilen:
## Was ist Hodenkrebs?
Hodenkrebs - auch Hodenkarzinom genannt - ist eine seltene Krebsart, die in den Hoden entsteht. Die Hoden sind das Fortpflanzungsorgan innerhalb des Hodensacks, die Spermien und das Hormon Testosteron produzieren.
Dies ist die häufigste Krebsform bei jungen Männern im Alter zwischen 15 und 35 Jahren. Die am häufigsten auftretenden Symptome von Hodenkrebs sind ein schmerzfreier Knoten oder die Schwellung eines Hodens und das Gefühl von Schwere im Hodensack. Der Krebs kann jedoch auch keinerlei Symptome aufweisen.
Die primäre Behandlung sieht die chirurgische Entfernung des Krebses vor. Andere Behandlungsoptionen basierend generell auf dem Stadium des Hodenkrebses. Viele Menschen erholen sich gut nach einer entsprechenden Behandlung.
## Was ist das Risiko von Hodenkrebs?
Krebs entsteht, wenn eine Gruppe abnormer Zellen unkontrolliert wächst. Diese Zellen zerstören die umliegenden gesunden Zellen und können in weitere Teile des Körpers streuen. **Hodenkrebs tritt auf, wenn dieser Prozess in den Hoden abläuft. Obwohl Hodenkrebs nicht oft vorkommt, so handelt es sich doch um die häufigste solide Krebsform bei Männern zwischen 20 und 35 Jahren. **
Ältere Männer und jüngere Jungen können diesen Krebs ebenfalls entwickeln, auch wenn dies seltener vorkommt. Die Ursache für Hodenkrebs ist nicht bekannt. Personen, in deren Familie bereits Fälle von Hodenkrebs bekannt sind, entwickeln ihn mit höherer Wahrscheinlichkeit. Personen mit [HIV](https://ada.com/de/conditions/acute-hiv-infection/), Personen, die als Kind an einem [Hodenhochstand](https://ada.com/de/conditions/cryptorchidism/) litten (eine Erkrankung, bei der sich der Hoden nicht im Hodensack befindet) oder die eine Chromosomenstörung, das so genannte Klinefelter-Syndrom, haben, haben ebenfalls ein erhöhtes Risiko für Hodenkrebs.
## Was sind Hodenkrebs-Symptome?
Die häufigsten Symptome sind ein schmerzloser Knoten oder eine Schwellung des Hodens.
  * ein Gefühl der Schwere,
  * Schmerzen
  * oder eine Schwellung des Hodensacks.


Einige Menschen verspüren den Schmerz und die Schwere im unteren Bauchbereich. Manche Betroffene können Brustgewebe entwickeln, was jedoch recht ungewöhnlich ist.
Wenn Du Dir unsicher bist, ob diese Beschwerden auf Dich zutreffen, starte eine 
## Wie wird Hodenkrebs diagnostiziert?
Die Diagnose erfolgt basierend auf der körperlichen Untersuchung des Hodensacks, auf Bluttests und einer Ultraschall-Untersuchung des Hodensacks sowie einer Computertomographie des Bauchs. Die Diagnose wird bestätigt, wenn eine kleine Probe (Biopsie) des Hodensacks auf Krebs hinweist.
## Wie wird Hodenkrebs behandelt?
Die Behandlung hängt von der Größe des Krebses, der spezifischen Krebsart und davon ab, ob er bereits an andere Stellen im Körper gestreut hat.
Im Einzelfall sollte man stets ärztlichen Rat aufsuchen. Diese Behandlungen können zu Unfruchtbarkeit führen. Wenn Betroffene für die Zukunft noch einen Kinderwunsch haben, ist die Einlagerung der Spermien in einer Samenbank möglich. Emotionale Unterstützung im Rahmen einer individuellen Beratung oder Hilfegruppe hilft den betroffenen Personen, mit der Diagnose und mit einer etwaigen Behandlung zurechtzukommen.
## Was ist die Prognose bei Hodenkrebs?
Die Prognose hängt vom Stadium und vom Art des Hodenkrebses ab. Viele Menschen werden früh diagnostiziert, sprechen gut auf die Behandlung an und können geheilt werden.
## Wie kann man Hodenkrebs vorbeugen?
Eine Selbstuntersuchung der Hoden

# What can I do if Ada missed something?
We're always working to improve Ada's medical content and technology through rigorous internal and external reviews. Our Medical Knowledge Team, consisting of doctors from over 20 countries and various specialties, ensures Ada is accurate, safe, and comprehensive and minimizes bias by utilizing their diverse expertise and experiences.
If Ada misses something significant, we have strict prompt review and correction protocols. Please let us know if you believe Ada's results were incorrect. [Provide your User ID](https://ada.com/help/360000308665/) or contact us using the email linked to your Ada account.
Remember, Ada's information is not a diagnosis and shouldn't replace professional medical advice. It offers possible explanations for symptoms and suggests care options, but it's not a substitute for a doctor's diagnosis. Your feedback helps us make Ada better for everyone.
Have more questions? [Submit a request](https://ada.com/contact/support/)

# Einwilligung in die Verarbeitung Ihrer Gesundheitsdaten zur Bereitstellung unserer Services
Stand: 13. November 2019
Durch Setzen des Häkchens willigen Sie in die Verarbeitung Ihrer personenbezogenen Gesundheitsdaten wie Geschlecht, Geburtsdatum, allgemeine Ihre Gesundheit betreffende Informationen, Symptome, mögliche Ursachen von Symptomen, Allergien, Schwangerschaftsstatus und die damit zusammenhängende medizinische Vorgeschichte ein, damit wir Ihnen unsere Services, d.h. Auswertungen Ihrer persönlichen Gesundheitsdaten und Empfehlungen zur Verfügung stellen können. Ohne Ihre Einwilligung in die Verarbeitung dieser Daten ist es nicht möglich, unsere App zu nutzen, da wir ohne sie keine Auswertungen und Empfehlungen vornehmen können.
Weitere Zwecke, für die wir diese Daten nutzen, betreffen die Analyse von Fallinformationen zur Gewährleistung hoher Qualitäts- und Sicherheitsstandards unseres medizinischen Bewertungssystems und die Erstellung anonymisierter Statistiken zur geographischen Verbreitung bestimmter Krankheitssymptome und Erkrankungen.
Weitere Informationen darüber wie und zu welchen Zwecken wir Ihre personenbezogenen Daten verarbeiten, finden Sie in unserer [Datenschutzerklärung](https://ada.com/de/privacy-policy/).

# Vitamin B12 Deficiency
Written by [Ada’s Medical Knowledge Team](https://ada.com/team/medical/)
Updated on April 7, 2025 at 4:00 PM GMT+2

## What is vitamin B12 deficiency?
Vitamin B12 deficiency occurs when there are inadequate levels of the vitamin B12 in the body.
A lack of vitamin B12 can cause anemia and other health problems.[1](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [2](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2") Anemia is a condition where the body either cannot make enough healthy red blood cells or cannot produce enough of the substance [hemoglobin](https://ada.com/biomarkers/hemoglobin/) that allows red blood cells to transport oxygen around the body.
There are several different types of anemia, each with their own causes and symptoms. For example, vitamin B12 deficiency can cause megaloblastic anemia, a condition where the red blood cells are larger than normal and cannot function properly. [2](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2") [3](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3")
For many people, a balanced and varied diet provides all the vitamin B12 they need.[2](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2") Good sources of vitamin B12 include meat, fish, eggs and dairy products.
Despite the availability of vitamin B12 in a balanced diet, deficiency is not all that uncommon, particularly among people over 50 years of age, premenopausal women and people who follow strict vegan diets. [4](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:4 "See Footnote 4") [5](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:5 "See Footnote 5")
Worried you may have vitamin B12 deficiency
Low levels of vitamin B12 may be the result of a number of different factors and conditions. One of the most common causes of vitamin B12 deficiency is pernicious anemia, a condition where a person’s immune system mistakenly reduces their ability to absorb the vitamin. Less common causes of deficiency include conditions affecting the stomach or intestines that interfere with absorption of vitamin B12, inadequate dietary intake, and certain medications. [1](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1")
Symptoms of vitamin B12 deficiency
If left untreated, the symptoms of vitamin B12 deficiency tend to worsen and irreversible problems involving the nerves and brain may develop. The risk of experiencing a number of serious complications, including heart failure, may also increase. [3](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3") [6](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6") For this reason, it is important to seek medical advice without delay should any of these symptoms be present.
## Symptoms of Vitamin B12 deficiency
A person with vitamin B12 deficiency may notice general symptoms of [anemia](https://ada.com/conditions/anemia/) as well as symptoms that are more specific to the condition.
Symptoms more specific to a vitamin B12 deficiency include: [2](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2") [7](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:7 "See Footnote 7") [6](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6") [8](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:8 "See Footnote 8")
  * Pale yellow skin color
  * Painful, red tongue
  * Mouth ulcers and canker sores
  * Constipation
  * Pins and needles, numbness or other strange sensations in the hands, legs or feet
  * Vision disturbances
  * Difficulty walking and balance problems
  * Perceptible differences in mood, thoughts, feelings and behavior
  * Confusion and difficulty thinking. In severe cases, dementia
  * Memory loss
  * Irritability
  * [Depression](https://ada.com/signs-of-depression/)
  * Psychosis [3](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3")


The symptoms of vitamin B12 deficiency can develop slowly and worsen over time.[6](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6")
Because of the wide range of possible symptoms, many of which can also occur as a result of other conditions, vitamin B12 deficiency may not be recognized immediately.[8](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:8 "See Footnote 8") If a person has any reason to suspect the condition, it is important that they inform their healthcare practitioner.
In babies,[7](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:7 "See Footnote 7")
Worried you may have vitamin B12 deficiency? Check your symptoms using the free [symptom checker](https://ada.com/app/) works before you try it for yourself.
### General symptoms caused by anemia
A person with vitamin B12 deficiency may also notice general symptoms of anemia[6](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6")
  * Fatigue
  * Lethargy
  * Breathlessness
  * Faintness
  * Headaches


Less common symptoms of anemia may include: [2](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2")
  * Paleness
  * Palpitations
  * Tinnitus (ringing in the ears)
  * Loss of appetite
  * Altered sense of taste
  * Unexplained weight loss

## What causes vitamin B12 deficiency?
Pernicious anemia is a common cause of vitamin B12 deficiency. There are several other possible causes of the deficiency, but they tend to be less common. [2](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2")
### Pernicious anemia
In order for vitamin B12 to be absorbed by the body, it needs to be combined with a protein called intrinsic factor in the stomach. This protein is produced by cells in the stomach lining. In people with pernicious anemia, the body’s immune system mistakenly attacks these cells,[2](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2") [6](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6")
Pernicious anemia is an autoimmune condition that most commonly affects people over 50 years old, and women seem to be more likely to develop it. Pernicious anemia is thought to run in families and seems to affect people who have other autoimmune conditions, such as Hashimoto’s thyroiditis and Addison’s disease, more often than those who do not. A healthcare practitioner can order a blood test to check for pernicious anemia. [2](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2") [6](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6")
### Conditions affecting the stomach and intestines
People who have certain conditions that affect the stomach and intestines, or have had certain types of surgery, may be at risk of vitamin B12 deficiency. [2](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2") [6](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6")
  * Stomach conditions.[gastritis](https://ada.com/conditions/chronic-gastritis/), which causes thinning of the stomach lining, infection with Helicobacter pylori bacteria, and a genetic condition that causes a lack of intrinsic factor can all cause vitamin B12 deficiency.
  * Intestinal conditions.[Crohn’s disease, a condition that causes inflammation of the lining of the digestive tract](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/), celiac disease, [7](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:7 "See Footnote 7") chronic tropical sprue and a number of other conditions may lead to vitamin B12 deficiency.
  * Surgery.


Worried you may have vitamin B12 deficiency
### Medications
Some medicines can interfere with the absorption of vitamin B12,[7](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:7 "See Footnote 7") colchicine and certain anticonvulsant drugs. [2](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2")
In addition, the long-term use of certain medicines that are used to treat stomach conditions, such as heartburn and [peptic ulcers](https://ada.com/conditions/peptic-ulcer-disease/), [9](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:9 "See Footnote 9") can worsen an existing vitamin B12 deficiency, but do not cause it.[2](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2") [6](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6")
Good to know:
### Inadequate dietary intake
Though fairly uncommon, some people may develop vitamin B12 deficiency as a result of low levels in their daily diet.[2](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2") [6](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6") Good sources of vitamin B12 include:
  * Meat
  * Fish
  * Eggs
  * Dairy products


In addition, some breakfast cereals, soy products and other foods are fortified with vitamin B12.[1](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [7](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:7 "See Footnote 7")
In healthy people, the body tends to have a store of vitamin B12[6](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6") [10](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:10 "See Footnote 10")
It is important that people making long-term dietary changes, for example becoming vegan, eat food products that have been fortified with [vitamin B12](https://ada.com/micronutrients/vitamin-b12/) or take a supplement to reduce the risk of developing a deficiency. [8](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:8 "See Footnote 8")
## Diagnosis of vitamin B12 deficiency
A doctor will typically take the person’s medical history and perform a physical examination.
If they suspect a vitamin B12 deficiency, they will usually request [blood tests](https://ada.com/blood-test-results/) to be done. These tests can measure levels of vitamin B12 and folic acid, as well as the size and [concentration of hemoglobin](https://ada.com/hemoglobin-levels/) within the person’s red blood cells. [6](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6")
### Drawbacks of blood tests for vitamin B12 deficiency
Some people experience symptoms of vitamin B12 deficiency despite their blood tests indicating normal levels.[6](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6") In addition, the range of normal levels may differ between laboratories. 
For these reasons, healthcare practitioners will usually consider signs and symptoms, as well as the results of the blood tests
[Read more about Blood Test Results »](https://ada.com/blood-test-results/)
### Tests to identify the cause
If vitamin B12 deficiency is suspected or confirmed, further tests may be required to identify the cause. This will help to determine the recommended course of treatment.[6](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6") and other conditions.
Some people may be referred to specialists[1](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1")
### Ruling out folate deficiency
A deficiency of folate, the nutrient also known as folic acid or vitamin B9, good sources of which include foods like broccoli, asparagus, peas and brown rice, can cause some of the same symptoms[6](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6") For this reason, a doctor will typically examine the levels of folate in blood tests when checking for vitamin B12 deficiency. [3](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3")
Taking a lot of folic acid can mask the symptoms of a vitamin B12 deficiency, so in cases where folate deficiency is suspected, a doctor will usually test for vitamin B12 deficiency before prescribing medication. [10](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:10 "See Footnote 10")
[Read more about Folate Deficiency »](https://ada.com/conditions/folate-deficiency/)
### Functional vitamin B12 deficiency
Sometimes blood tests will show normal serum levels of vitamin B12, but a person may experience symptoms and complications related to a deficiency. This can be known as fuctional vitamin B12 deficiency. In these cases, there may be an issue with the processing of vitamin B12 in the body.
Like most other cases of vitamin B12 deficiency, the condition can be treated with high doses of vitamin B12.[6](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6") However, a prolonged functional vitamin B12 deficiency can lead to the same problems as a regular vitamin B12 deficiency. 
Worried you may have vitamin B12 deficiency
## Treatment of Vitamin B12 deficiency
Treatment will depend on the reasons for the vitamin B12 deficiency.[6](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6")
A doctor may recommend having high-dose injections of vitamin B12, usually in a form called hydroxocobalamin, every second day for two weeks, or until symptoms have cleared.
If the cause of the deficiency is dietary,[6](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6") They may also refer the person to a dietician for advice on ways to increase vitamin B12 intake in their diet. [1](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [3](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3")
In cases where the deficiency is not related to a person’s diet,[6](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6")
People who have symptoms that affect their nervous system,[2](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2") [6](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6")
Vitamin B12 injections typically do not have any side-effects other than a small amount of discomfort where the needle is inserted. [2](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2")
Follow-up blood tests[6](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6") [3](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3") [10](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:10 "See Footnote 10")
In most cases, a vitamin B12 deficiency is easy to treat and complications are rare.[1](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") However, in some cases, particularly where there has been a severe or prolonged deficiency, nerve damage may be permanent and irreversible. [2](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2") [3](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3") [9](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:9 "See Footnote 9")
Good to know:
## Prevention of vitamin B12 deficiency
While it may not be possible to prevent vitamin B12 deficiency in all cases, steps can be taken to reduce the likelihood of the condition developing.
A person should speak to their healthcare practitioner[8](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:8 "See Footnote 8")
  * Use a proton pump inhibitor on a long-term basis
  * Use an H2 blocker on a long-term basis
  * Take metformin for their [diabetes](https://ada.com/conditions/diabetes/)
  * Are strict vegans
  * Have conditions affecting the stomach
  * Have had gastric surgery or surgery on the small intestine


People with conditions that may interfere with the absorption of the vitamin, such as [celiac disease](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/) and Crohn’s disease, as well as those over the age of 50, should also discuss their vitamin B12 needs with a healthcare practitioner. [8](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:8 "See Footnote 8")
It is recommended that strict vegans (and sometimes vegetarians) and people over 50 include breads, cereals or other food products that have been fortified with vitamin B12 in their diet, and/or take a supplement. [8](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:8 "See Footnote 8")
## Complications of vitamin B12 deficiency
Occasionally, a vitamin B12 deficiency can cause complications.[6](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6") [3](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3")
  * Neurological problems.
  * Infertility.
  * Stomach cancer.[stomach cancer](https://ada.com/conditions/stomach-cancer/) may be increased.
  * Neural tube defects.


In addition, anemia of all kinds can sometimes cause serious heart and lung complications.[3](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3")
Read more about [anemia complications »](https://ada.com/conditions/anemia/#complications)
To prevent complications, people who suspect they may have a vitamin B12 deficiency are advised to consult a qualified healthcare practitioner without delay.
## Other names for vitamin B12 deficiency
  * Cobalamin deficiency


## Find out more about your symptoms
## Vitamin B12 deficiency FAQs
Q: Are vegetarians and vegans at risk of vitamin B12 deficiency?  
A:[4](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:4 "See Footnote 4") [6](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6") To minimize the likelihood of a deficiency, it is recommended that strict vegans and vegetarians include foods that have been fortified with vitamin B12 in their daily diet. Examples include certain breads, soy products and cereals, as well as certain yeast extracts. It may also be necessary to take a daily supplement. 
Q: Can vitamin B12 deficiency cause depression?  
A:[3](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3") It is important to remember that depression can be caused by a number of different factors. If a person suspects that a vitamin B12 deficiency may be implicated in their depressed mood, they are advised to speak to a healthcare practitioner.
Q: Is there a link between alcohol and vitamin B12 deficiency?  
A:[11](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:11 "See Footnote 11") [12](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:12 "See Footnote 12") [13](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-b12-deficiency/#fn:13 "See Footnote 13")

# Trichomoniasis Test
Written by [Ada’s Medical Knowledge Team](https://ada.com/team/medical/)
Updated on September 12, 2024 at 5:00 PM GMT+3

Trichomoniasis
Regardless, it's still important to be aware of trichomoniasis and to know if you are infected. 
A test is the only way to ensure you aren't infected with the parasite that causes trichomoniasis. Getting tested for trichomoniasis is a good way to control your sexual health while avoiding complications due to the infection and preventing the parasite from spreading to your sexual partners.
Concerned that you or a loved one my have a STD
## What is a trichomoniasis test?
A trichomoniasis test[trichomoniasis](https://ada.com/conditions/trichomonas-vulvovaginitis/).   
  
Trichomoniasis is caused by a parasiteTrichomonas vaginalis
The symptoms of trichomoniasis are a bit different depending on if you’re a man or a woman. Still, symptoms primarily consist of inflammation of the genitals and pain or discomfort when peeing or having sex. 
Trichomoniasis can also cause abnormal discharges. For women, the discharge may be thick, thin, or frothy with a yellow-green color. For men, the discharge may be thin and white.
In almost half of all cases, trichomoniasis doesn't cause any symptoms, so it's very important to practice safe sex and get tested regularly. By getting a trichomoniasis test, you can be sure of your status and keep yourself and your sexual partners healthy. [1](https://ada.com/sexual-health/trichomoniasis-test/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [2](https://ada.com/sexual-health/trichomoniasis-test/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2") [3](https://ada.com/sexual-health/trichomoniasis-test/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3")
A trichomoniasis test can be used for several purposes: [1](https://ada.com/sexual-health/trichomoniasis-test/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1")
  * Screening of people without symptoms: this is mostly done for people at high risk of contracting trichomoniasis. 
  * Diagnosis of trichomoniasis in people that experience symptoms: trichomoniasis is quite difficult to differentiate from other STDs. Only a test can tell for sure. 
  * Monitoring to see if trichomoniasis treatment has been effective: a previous trichomoniasis infection doesn’t make you immune. You could get reinfected after treatment if your sexual partner hasn’t been treated. 


As with most STD tests, trichomoniasis tests are easy to take and can be done relatively quickly. Your test results can come back within an hour or a few days, depending on which test you take.
Concerned that you or a loved one my have a STD
### How to test for trichomoniasis?
If you're sexually active, getting tested regularly for trichomoniasis is important, as you can pass the parasite along to your partner, even without symptoms. A test will come back positive if you have trichomoniasis, even if you don’t have symptoms. 
There are various ways to get testedWomen[2](https://ada.com/sexual-health/trichomoniasis-test/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2") [4](https://ada.com/sexual-health/trichomoniasis-test/#fn:4 "See Footnote 4") [5](https://ada.com/sexual-health/trichomoniasis-test/#fn:5 "See Footnote 5")
  * A nucleic acid amplification test
  * A rapid at-home trichomonas test
  * You can do this test at home with a blood prick test and a urine sample


The trichomoniasis test for men[2](https://ada.com/sexual-health/trichomoniasis-test/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2") [4](https://ada.com/sexual-health/trichomoniasis-test/#fn:4 "See Footnote 4") [5](https://ada.com/sexual-health/trichomoniasis-test/#fn:5 "See Footnote 5")
  * A swab
  * A home urine test
  * As described above, a test at home


## What to do if I test positive for trichomoniasis?
There are 3 steps to take if your test results come back positive:[1](https://ada.com/sexual-health/trichomoniasis-test/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [4](https://ada.com/sexual-health/trichomoniasis-test/#fn:4 "See Footnote 4")
  1. Start treatment as early as possible with antibiotics: if you’re allergic to certain antibiotics or are pregnant, it’s important to let your doctor know so that treatment can be adjusted to your personal needs. 
  2. Notify your sexual partners: trichomoniasis can spread through sexual contact and often shows no symptoms. Notifying your sexual partners helps protect them and helps stop the parasite from spreading. It also decreases the chances of you getting reinfected by your sexual partner. 
  3. Monitor the outcome of your treatment: your doctor will test you again after treatment to make sure that the parasite is gone and that you haven’t been reinfected. Once you’ve tested negative, you don’t have the parasite anymore, so you can’t infect others. 


## Can a man have trichomoniasis and test negative?
Diagnosing trichomoniasis in men is usually more difficult than it is in women
As they are less likely to experience symptoms, men often don’t get a trichomoniasis test done. It's important to note that even when there aren't any symptoms present, men can still develop complications from untreated trichomoniasis and infect others. [1](https://ada.com/sexual-health/trichomoniasis-test/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1")
The parasite can be missed in men because they usually get tested with a trichomoniasis urine test. This is because a significant amount of the parasite must be present for the test to pick it up, and urine can be quite dilute. For that reason, it’s important to collect your sample in the morning, as the first urine of the day is less diluted and will have a higher probability of showing the parasite if it's present. [4](https://ada.com/sexual-health/trichomoniasis-test/#fn:4 "See Footnote 4")

# Cholecystitis
Written by [Ada’s Medical Knowledge Team](https://ada.com/team/medical/)
Updated on February 15, 2022 at 10:00 AM GMT+2

## What is cholecystitis?
Cholecystitis is the medical term for inflammation of the gallbladder.
The gallbladder stores bile, which is a liquid produced by the liver to help digest fatty foods. After eating, the gallbladder typically squeezes bile down the bile tract and into the intestines. In most, but not all cases, acute cholecystitis is caused by [gallstones](https://ada.com/conditions/symptomatic-cholelithiasis/) from the gallbladder blocking the drainage of bile. The condition often causes sudden, lasting pain in the upper or upper-right areas of the belly.[2](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2")
Treatment, which often requires going to a hospital, may initially involve pain-relief measures, fluids and antibiotics. In most cases, the gallbladder will need to be removed in a surgical procedure called a cholecystectomy. [3](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3")
With appropriate treatment, the outlook for uncomplicated cases of cholecystitis is generally very good, and most people recover well.[4](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:4 "See Footnote 4")
Feeling unwell? Get a symptom assessment with the 
## Cholecystitis symptoms
Severe pain in the upper or upper-right area of the belly is the most common symptom[5](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:5 "See Footnote 5")
Other symptoms associated with gallbladder inflammation may include: [2](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2") [3](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3") [5](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:5 "See Footnote 5")
  * Loss of appetite
  * Nausea
  * Vomiting
  * Sweating
  * Fever
  * In some cases, yellowing of the skin and the whites of the eyes, known as jaundice


Symptoms can vary, depending on the individual person and what is causing the cholecystitis. They may be worse after a meal. [diabetes](https://ada.com/conditions/diabetes/), may experience tenderness rather than pain and other vague symptoms, such as feeling unwell and weak. [5](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:5 "See Footnote 5") [6](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6")
Good to know:[5](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:5 "See Footnote 5")
If fever and/or jaundice is present or symptoms are severe, it is recommended that you seek medical care without delay.
## Causes of gallbladder inflammation
There are two main causes of acute gallbladder inflammation: [2](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2") [6](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6") [7](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:7 "See Footnote 7") [8](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:8 "See Footnote 8")
  * In cases described as calculous cholecystitis,
  * In cases described as acalculous cholecystitis,[4](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:4 "See Footnote 4")


### Calculous cholecystitis risk factors
Gallstones are the main risk factor for developing cholecystitis.[2](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2") [4](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:4 "See Footnote 4") [7](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:7 "See Footnote 7") [9](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:9 "See Footnote 9")
  * Being female
  * Increasing age
  * A family history of cholecystitis
  * Having European, Native American or Hispanic heritage
  * Being overweight or obese
  * [Pregnancy](https://ada.com/conditions/pregnancy/)
  * Certain medical conditions, including [Crohn’s disease](https://ada.com/conditions/crohns-disease/)
  * Rapid weight loss, e.g. as experienced after weight-loss surgery or intense dieting


### Acalculous cholecystitis risk factors
Cholecystitis without gallstones, which is far less common, is generally associated with factors that include: [10](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:10 "See Footnote 10") [8](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:8 "See Footnote 8")
  * Failure of multiple organs
  * Serious burns or other injuries
  * Intravenous feeding (parenteral nutrition) for long periods of time
  * Being in intensive care
  * [Cardiovascular disease](https://ada.com/cardiovascular-disease-risk-factors/)
  * [Diabetes](https://ada.com/conditions/diabetes/)
  * [Sepsis](https://ada.com/conditions/sepsis/)
  * Advanced stages of HIV


Good to know:
## Diagnosis
As a first step, a doctor will assess the person’s symptoms, take their medical history and perform a physical examination.
The doctor might press on the upper-right area of the belly, just below the ribcage, and ask the person to take a deep breath, checking for what is known as Murphy’s sign. Pain that is felt during this test may indicate that the gallbladder is inflamed. [2](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2") [3](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3")
The doctor may order a urine test to check for signs of kidney problems and [blood tests](https://ada.com/blood-test-results/) to check for signs of infection or problems in the liver or pancreas. They may also request that an ultrasound scan computed tomography (CT) scan or other imaging tests be performed to examine the gallbladder and other parts of the abdomen and confirm the diagnosis. [6](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6") [11](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:11 "See Footnote 11")
It is important to rule out other conditions that may sometimes cause symptoms similar to gallbladder inflammation, including: 
  * [Appendicitis](https://ada.com/conditions/acute-appendicitis/)
  * [Gastritis](https://ada.com/conditions/acute-gastritis/)
  * [Pancreatitis](https://ada.com/conditions/acute-pancreatitis/)
  * [Kidney stones](https://ada.com/conditions/nephrolithiasis/)


Good to know:[2](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2")
If you are worried that you or someone you know may have this condition, use the 
### Imaging tests
Imaging tests for suspected cholecystitis may include the following: [12](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:12 "See Footnote 12") [2](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2") [3](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3") [9](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:9 "See Footnote 9") [11](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:11 "See Footnote 11") [13](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:13 "See Footnote 13") [14](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:14 "See Footnote 14") [15](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:15 "See Footnote 15")
Abdominal ultrasound.
CT scan.
MRI.
Hepatobiliary scintigraphy.
Cholangiography.[16](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:16 "See Footnote 16") This test may form part of a procedure called an endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP), where a thin, flexible tube called an endoscope is used to diagnose and remove gallstones that have become stuck in bile ducts.
Plain X-rays.
## Treatment of gallbladder inflammation
While it depends on the cause and severity of the condition, initial treatment of cholecystitis will usually involve pain-relief measures, intravenous fluids to prevent dehydration and sometimes antibiotics. Generally, surgical removal of the gallbladder will be necessary, and it may be recommended that this take place within the next day or two.[17](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:17 "See Footnote 17") [2](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2") [3](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3") [6](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6")
In mild, uncomplicated cases, it may sometimes be possible for a person to receive initial treatment without a hospital stay and then go to hospital to prepare for surgery on the date determined by their doctor. However, in more severe cases of gallbladder inflammation, immediate hospitalization may be needed. [17](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:17 "See Footnote 17") [9](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:9 "See Footnote 9")
### Cholecystectomy
Surgery to remove the gallbladder, called cholecystectomy, is the standard treatment[2](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2") [7](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:7 "See Footnote 7")
There are two types of gallbladder surgery: [3](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3") [9](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:9 "See Footnote 9") [13](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:13 "See Footnote 13") [18](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:18 "See Footnote 18") [19](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:19 "See Footnote 19") [20](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:20 "See Footnote 20") [21](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:21 "See Footnote 21")
Laparoscopic cholecystectomy.
Open cholecystectomy.
#### After gallbladder surgery
A person can live a normal, healthy life without their gallbladder.[2](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2") [9](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:9 "See Footnote 9") [13](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:13 "See Footnote 13") [21](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:21 "See Footnote 21") [22](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:22 "See Footnote 22")
### Non-surgical treatment
In cases where a person is unable to undergo surgery because the risks are too great, doctors might insert a catheter into the gallbladder to drain it and reduce the inflammation – this is called a percutaneous cholecystostomy.[17](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:17 "See Footnote 17") [6](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6")
In cases where surgery is not immediately possible, the gallbladder may also be drained using a procedure called an endoscopic ultrasound-guided transmural cholecystostomy.[17](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:17 "See Footnote 17")
[Read about treatment of gallstones, the most common cause of gallbladder inflammation »](https://ada.com/conditions/symptomatic-cholelithiasis/#gallstones-treatment)
## Complications of gallbladder inflammation
If left untreated, cholecystitis can result in serious complications, some of which may be life-threatening. Possible complications include: [2](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2") [24](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:24 "See Footnote 24")
  * Gangrenous cholecystitis,[25](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:25 "See Footnote 25")
  * Gallbladder perforation,


[Read about other possible complications of gallbladder disease »](https://ada.com/conditions/symptomatic-cholelithiasis/#complications)
In these cases, emergency treatment is usually required.[6](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6")
  * Sudden, severe pain in the belly, which worsens
  * High fever
  * Chills, shivering and sweating
  * Vomiting
  * Rapid heartbeat


### Chronic cholecystitis
Sometimes, gallbladder inflammation persists for a long period of time. In such cases, the term ‘chronic cholecystitis’ is used. Chronic gallbladder inflammation is almost always caused by [gallstones](https://ada.com/conditions/symptomatic-cholelithiasis/). With repeat episodes of acute cholecystitis, sometimes called gallbladder attacks, which occur in chronic cholecystitis, the gallbladder can become damaged, and its functioning may be impaired. Treatment typically involves surgery to remove the gallbladder (cholecystectomy). [26](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:26 "See Footnote 26") [27](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:27 "See Footnote 27")
Chronic gallbladder inflammation may increase the risk of [gallbladder cancer](https://ada.com/conditions/gallbladder-cancer/). If gallbladder inflammation is known or suspected, it is important to seek medical treatment to minimize the risk of complications occurring.
### Post-cholecystectomy syndrome
After having their gallbladder removed, an estimated 1 in 10 people develop what is known as postcholecystectomy syndrome (PCS). They may experience a number of symptoms associated with gallbladder disease, as well as symptoms related to removal of the gallbladder. [13](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:13 "See Footnote 13")
[Read more about post-cholecystectomy syndrome »](https://ada.com/conditions/symptomatic-cholelithiasis/#complications)
## Prevention
While it may not be possible to prevent gallbladder inflammation, taking steps to reduce the risk of developing gallstones, the major cause of gallbladder inflammation, may be helpful. [2](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2")
[Read more about preventing gallstones »](https://ada.com/conditions/symptomatic-cholelithiasis/#prevention)
## Gallbladder inflammation in pregnancy
During pregnancy, a person’s risk of developing gallstones and, as a result, gallbladder inflammation, is increased. If cholecystitis occurs in pregnancy, surgery to remove the gallbladder may be necessary to avoid complications. This usually takes the form of a laparoscopic cholecystectomy and is generally considered to be safe at any stage of pregnancy. [28](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:28 "See Footnote 28") [29](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:29 "See Footnote 29") [30](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:30 "See Footnote 30")
Some doctors may prefer to treat a pregnant person with pain-relief measures, fluid replacement and antibiotics initially, recommending gallbladder surgery after the baby has been delivered. However, with delayed surgery, the risk of complications may be increased for both the mother and baby. [29](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:29 "See Footnote 29") [30](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:30 "See Footnote 30")
## Other names for cholecystitis
  * Gallbladder inflammation
  * Hot gallbladder (uncommon) [31](https://ada.com/conditions/cholecystitis/#fn:31 "See Footnote 31")

# How to keep taking care of yourself after the Ada app is removed in some countries
[Ada](https://ada.com/editorial/writers/ada/)
Published on March 16, 2023 at 1:00 AM GMT+2
For the past years, we've worked tirelessly to [receive a Class IIa medical device certification](https://ada.com/press/221215-ada-health-receives-eu-mdr-certification/), as this is a recognition of our commitment to safety and quality. However, to maintain this certification, the Ada app must meet specific requirements set forth by the EU. Let’s learn how these may affect you and how you can keep taking care of yourself after this. 
## What's changing?
On 16.03.2023, we'll remove the Ada app from the Apple Store and Google Play Store in the EU and European Economic Area (EEA) countries whose official languages we do not currently support. Shortly after that, we won't be able to provide assistance for the Ada app in those countries, except for the export and deletion of your personal data, as further explained below. 
## Why is it changing?
These changes are mandated by the European Medical Device Regulation (EU-MDR), so we're required to do this. 
## Who will be affected?
If you live in one of the following countries, you'll be affected by this change: Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Slovakia, Slovenia, Sweden, Switzerland,Türkiye.
## What are the next steps?
  * When we remove the Ada app from the Apple Store and Google Play Store, it will remain on your device if you already have it installed. 
  * The Ada app will continue to function until our next major update.
  * If you delete your Ada app or change devices, you'll not be able to reinstall it.


## What happens to my data?
You'll have the right to export your personal data or delete your Ada account in accordance with our [Privacy Policy](https://ada.com/privacy-policy/) and as explained further below. You can only do this before the end of April when the Ada app will become critically outdated.
## Would you like to learn more about this? 
3 things to keep in mind:
  * You are not required to delete your Ada account. If the Ada app becomes available in your country, or if you move to another country where it's available, your account will remain accessible - except as otherwise required by any data protection laws and applicable data deletion requirements.
  * We're continually working on adding additional languages to the Ada app and are hoping to restore functionality in the affected countries soon. 
  * After we remove the Ada app from the Apple Store and Google Play Store, we'll continue to offer support and provide assistance in exporting or deleting your personal data. 


## How to keep taking care of yourself
  * Read the articles from the website created by our in-house doctors. 
  * Follow our health tips on 
  * Access our [Medical Library](https://ada.com/conditions/) to learn more about certain conditions.


Thank you for being a valued part of the Ada community, and keep taking care of yourself. If you have any further questions or concerns, please don't hesitate to contact us at

## 1. Informação geral sobre cookies
As cookies são pequenos ficheiros de texto que um website poderá colocar no seu dispositivo no decurso da sua primeira visita. As cookies ajudam o website a reconhecer o seu dispositivo nas suas subsequentes visitas. Nesta política, utilizamos o termo "cookies" para nos referirmos a todo e qualquer ficheiro que recolha informação desta forma.
As cookies servem muitas funções. Por exemplo, poderão ajudar-nos a recordar o seu nome de utilizador e preferências, analisar o desempenho do Website ou mesmo permitir que recomendemos o conteúdo que acreditamos ser mais relevante para si.

  * Marketing

# HPV (Human papillomavirus)
Written by [Ada’s Medical Knowledge Team](https://ada.com/team/medical/)
Updated on September 16, 2024 at 1:00 PM GMT+3
## On this page
  * [What is HPV?](https://ada.com/conditions/human-papillomavirus-hpv-infection/#what-is-hpv)
  * [How is HPV transmitted?](https://ada.com/conditions/human-papillomavirus-hpv-infection/#how-is-hpv-transmitted)
  * [What are the symptoms of HPV in females?](https://ada.com/conditions/human-papillomavirus-hpv-infection/#what-are-the-symptoms-of-hpv-in-females)
  * [What does HPV look like on a man?](https://ada.com/conditions/human-papillomavirus-hpv-infection/#what-does-hpv-look-like-on-a-man)
  * [What is the HPV vaccine?](https://ada.com/conditions/human-papillomavirus-hpv-infection/#what-is-the-hpv-vaccine)
  * [What are HPV vaccine side effects?](https://ada.com/conditions/human-papillomavirus-hpv-infection/#what-are-hpv-vaccine-side-effects)
  * [How to prevent an HPV infection?](https://ada.com/conditions/human-papillomavirus-hpv-infection/#how-to-prevent-an-hpv-infection)
  * [HPV FAQs](https://ada.com/conditions/human-papillomavirus-hpv-infection/#hpv-faqs)


* * *
Share this article:
HPV is a virus that currently ranks as the most common STD
Think you might have HPV
## What is HPV?
HPV stands for human papillomavirus, and is a term to describe a group of viruses that affect the skin. It’s a very common virus that gets transmitted easily. It doesn’t always cause symptoms, but in some cases, it may have serious consequences for your health. These consequences depend on the genetic variant (also called a strain) of HPV you’ve been infected with. While some strains clear on their own, others may cause genital warts or cancers. [1](https://ada.com/conditions/human-papillomavirus-hpv-infection/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1")
Concerned that you or a loved one may have HPVAda's symptom checker.
## How is HPV transmitted?
HPV is considered an [STD](https://ada.com/sexual-health/), as it is transmitted through sexual contact. You can get HPV by: [1](https://ada.com/conditions/human-papillomavirus-hpv-infection/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [2](https://ada.com/conditions/human-papillomavirus-hpv-infection/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2")
  * Having unprotected vaginal or anal sex
  * Having oral sex 
  * Sharing sex toys
  * Having skin-to-skin contact with the genital area of an infected person. 


Someone may have HPV without showing any symptoms. Even with a lack of symptoms, the virus can still be passed along through skin-to-skin contact with the genitalia. Condoms do offer some protection, although they can’t assure full protection as they don’t cover all the genital skin. [2](https://ada.com/conditions/human-papillomavirus-hpv-infection/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2")
## What are the symptoms of HPV in females?
Not everyone with an HPV infection will show HPV symptoms. In about 90% of all cases, the virus won’t cause any trouble and it will even go away on its own within two years with the help of your own immune system. However, a small percentage of people can suffer from various health problems caused by this virus, such as genital warts and cancer. [3](https://ada.com/conditions/human-papillomavirus-hpv-infection/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3")
HPV warts can vary in shape and size, but are usually shaped like a cauliflower. They can be flat, but may also appear as a raised spot on the skin, which is why some people may confuse the warts caused by HPV with pimples. As there are many different ways for genital warts to appear, it’s advised to have a check-up with your doctor if you’ve noticed any lumps or growths that are new in your genital area. [1](https://ada.com/conditions/human-papillomavirus-hpv-infection/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [3](https://ada.com/conditions/human-papillomavirus-hpv-infection/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3")
Besides genital warts, HPV can also cause cancer in the genital area. There may be years between the infection and the actual development of a cancer. It’s hard to predict who might possibly suffer from health problems caused by HPV, but in general it’s said that people who have a weakened immune system (such as people with an [HIV infection](https://ada.com/conditions/acute-hiv-infection/)) are more prone to develop cancers due to HPV. Cancers caused by this virus may include: [3](https://ada.com/conditions/human-papillomavirus-hpv-infection/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3") [4](https://ada.com/conditions/human-papillomavirus-hpv-infection/#fn:4 "See Footnote 4")
  * Cervical cancer
  * Cancer of the vulva or the vagina 
  * Cancer of the anus 


Another consequence that can be caused by HPV is throat cancer, also called oropharyngeal cancer. The presence of HPV in the mouth and throat caused by oral sex can cause this cancer to develop years after being infected with the virus. Whether or not you’ll develop throat cancer after having oral HPV probably depends on other factors as well, such as the strength of the immune system, your alcohol consumption, or smoking habits. Cancers in the throat which are caused by HPV can affect the tonsils, the throat or the base of the tongue. [3](https://ada.com/conditions/human-papillomavirus-hpv-infection/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3") [4](https://ada.com/conditions/human-papillomavirus-hpv-infection/#fn:4 "See Footnote 4")
Some strains of HPV are more likely to cause symptoms in the mouth. Besides cancers, this can also be under the form of HPV bumps on the lips or HPV bumps on the tongue. [5](https://ada.com/conditions/human-papillomavirus-hpv-infection/#fn:5 "See Footnote 5")
There has also been a link found between HPV and[ pregnancy issues](https://ada.com/conditions/pregnancy/#complications). Pregnant women are often more prone to infections as their immune system temporarily changes throughout their pregnancy. Getting infected with HPV during pregnancy may result in a number of consequences such as preterm birth, miscarriage, and low birth weight. [6](https://ada.com/conditions/human-papillomavirus-hpv-infection/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6")
Think you might have HPV
## What does HPV look like on a man?
HPV in men is transmitted the same way as it is in women. Men usually don’t have any symptoms when they are infected with HPV, and the infection usually goes away by itself. If HPV does cause symptoms, then these findings will be visible on the penis, scrotum, anus, mouth, or throat. The symptoms may include: 
  * HPV Warts 
  * Lumps 
  * Sores 
  * Growths 


It may be that there’s only one wart visible, or they can occur in a group, which is when people often talk about a HPV rash. 
HPV may also cause cancers of the penis, the anus and the throat in men. However it’s not common for these cancers to develop after a HPV infection. Men who receive anal sex and men with weakened immune systems may be more prone to develop cancers caused by the virus. 
## What is the HPV vaccine?
The HPV vaccine was created to prevent complications of HPV infections. It’s especially targeted at avoiding cervical and oropharyngeal cancers, although it may also [help to prevent genital warts](https://ada.com/conditions/genital-warts/). [8](https://ada.com/conditions/human-papillomavirus-hpv-infection/#fn:8 "See Footnote 8")
The usual HPV vaccine schedule starts with a first dose at age 9-12, and a second dose 6-12 months after the first dose. For those who are vaccinated after turning 15, a third dose should be given as well. Both men and women up until 26 are advised to get vaccinated, although it’s best to start the vaccine schedule before becoming sexually active, to avoid coming into contact with the virus before being vaccinated. After 26, it’s not recommended for everyone to get vaccinated. A healthcare specialist can provide you with more information on vaccination for your personal situation. [8](https://ada.com/conditions/human-papillomavirus-hpv-infection/#fn:8 "See Footnote 8")
## What are HPV vaccine side effects?
Although the HPV vaccine is proven to be very safe and has already been monitored for over 15 years, there are some possible mild side effects that can occur after vaccination: [8](https://ada.com/conditions/human-papillomavirus-hpv-infection/#fn:8 "See Footnote 8")
  * Pain, swelling, or redness where the injection was administered, 
  * Dizziness or fainting,
  * Nausea,
  * Headaches


These side effects are common for all vaccines and are of short duration.
## How to prevent an HPV infection?
HPV infections can be prevented in a number of ways: 
  * By getting vaccinated. The vaccine is recommended for pre-teens and can still be administered until 26 years old. It’s ideal to get vaccinated before becoming sexually active, so that you haven’t been exposed to the virus yet. 
  * By using condoms or dental dams when having sex. Although these precautions are effective and help protect you against other STDs such as [chlamydia](https://ada.com/conditions/chlamydia-infection/), [gonorrhea](https://ada.com/conditions/gonorrhea-infection/), [syphilis](https://ada.com/conditions/syphilis-infection/) and [trichomoniasis](https://ada.com/conditions/trichomonas-vulvovaginitis/) as well, they don’t completely rule out the possibility of getting infected as HPV can be present on the skin around the genitalia that isn’t covered by the condom. 
  * By limiting your number of sexual partners or by practising abstinence. 


Screening for HPV infections is an important strategy to prevent cervical cancer. This is because women with persistent HPV infections or a compromised immune system due to conditions such as HIV are more likely to develop cervical cancer. Early intervention could therefore help you protect yourself against progression to pre-cancer and cancer. There are two different tests that can be done at your healthcare provider: [9](https://ada.com/conditions/human-papillomavirus-hpv-infection/#fn:9 "See Footnote 9") [10](https://ada.com/conditions/human-papillomavirus-hpv-infection/#fn:10 "See Footnote 10")
  * A Pap smear test, which looks for changes in the cells of the cervix. These changed cells might grow out to be cervical cancer if they aren’t treated appropriately
  * A HPV test, which looks for the human papillomavirus in the cells. 


The CDC recommends that you start getting screened at age 21 with a pap smear test. You should repeat this process every 3 to 5 years, depending on the advice of your doctor. If you’re older than 65, your doctor may tell you that you don’t need to get screened anymore if you’ve never had anything unusual in your test results or if you’ve had your cervix removed. [10](https://ada.com/conditions/human-papillomavirus-hpv-infection/#fn:10 "See Footnote 10")
## Find out more about your symptoms
## HPV FAQs
Q: Can you get HPV without having sex?   
A: Yes, you can also get HPV from skin-to-skin contact of the genital area. 
Q: Do I automatically get HPV if my partner has it?  
A: It’s very likely that partners share HPV, as the virus can get transmitted very easily and is not visible in most cases.
Q: Is HPV herpes?   
A: Although both herpes and HPV are STDs that may cause skin lesions that look alike, they are both different viruses with different characteristics. 
Q: How to get rid of HPV?   
A: The immune system usually clears HPV 1-2 years after being infected. There is no treatment for HPV itself, although it is possible to treat the consequences of the virus.
Q: How often do HPV warts recur?   
A: Genital warts may come back regularly after treatment. How often they do come back isn’t clear, but they may come back more in people with a weakened immune system. 
Q: Does HPV go away?   
A: The vast majority of cases clear within 1-2 years after infection. 
Q: How long can HPV be dormant?   
A: HPV can be dormant for years before causing problems like genital warts or cancers.
