# Signs of Postpartum Depression
Written by [Ada’s Medical Knowledge Team](https://ada.com/team/medical/)
Updated on October 28, 2021 at 3:58 PM GMT+2
## On this page
  * [What is postpartum depression?](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#what-is-postpartum-depression)
  * [What are the signs of postpartum depression (PPD)?](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#what-are-the-signs-of-postpartum-depression-ppd)
    * [Postpartum depression signs in fathers](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#postpartum-depression-signs-in-fathers)
  * [Risk factors](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#risk-factors)
  * [Postpartum depression diagnosis and treatment](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#postpartum-depression-diagnosis-and-treatment)
  * [Postpartum psychosis](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#postpartum-psychosis)
  * [FAQ](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#faq)


* * *
Share this article:
## What is postpartum depression?
Also known as postnatal [depression](https://ada.com/conditions/depressive-episode/), postpartum depression (PPD) is a type of depression that can occur with having a baby. PPD is much more severe than the mild “baby blues” that many new mothers experience for a few days or a couple of weeks after giving birth to their child. Postpartum depression is a serious medical conditionoften requires treatment[1](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [2](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2") [3](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3") [4](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#fn:4 "See Footnote 4")
Depression after the birth of a child is relatively commonmay be difficult to recognize[5](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#fn:5 "See Footnote 5") [2](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2") [4](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#fn:4 "See Footnote 4")
Postpartum depression can also affect partnerscan affect any new parent,[1](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [2](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2")
Postpartum depression may occur together with a number of other conditions, e.g. [anxiety](https://ada.com/conditions/generalized-anxiety-disorder/) or another depressive disorder, [diabetes](https://ada.com/conditions/diabetes/) or [thyroiditis](https://ada.com/conditions/thyroiditis/). The relationship between depression and other conditions is complex. [6](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6")
Good to know:[miscarriage](https://ada.com/conditions/miscarriage/) or abortion. [7](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#fn:7 "See Footnote 7")
Feeling unwell? Get a symptom assessment with the symptom checker works before you try it for yourself.
## What are the signs of postpartum depression (PPD)?
A parent with postnatal depression will often start to experience symptoms within the first month of having a child. However, symptoms can develop any time in the first 12 months, e.g. after four or six months. [8](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#fn:8 "See Footnote 8") Symptoms of depression may also develop [during the pregnancy itself](https://ada.com/conditions/pregnancy/), before delivery. Signs of postpartum depression are generally present for more than two weeks.
While they may vary from person to person, as well as differ in form and severity, some of the more common signs and symptoms of postnatal depression, like other types of depression, include: [5](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#fn:5 "See Footnote 5") [2](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2") [3](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3")
  * Persistent low mood; this may take the form of sadness, hopelessness, emptiness, irritability, frustration, anger, a feeling of being overwhelmed, or other negative emotions
  * Loss of interest or pleasure in activities that used to be enjoyable, including sex
  * Strong feelings of guilt or worthlessness
  * Tiredness and lack of energy and motivation
  * Trouble concentrating and making decisions
  * Memory problems
  * Overwhelming worry or anxiety
  * Restlessness or trouble sitting still
  * Withdrawal from loved ones
  * Disrupted sleep patterns, including difficulty falling asleep or sleeping too much
  * Changes in appetite
  * Persistent headaches, other pains, or digestive trouble without a clear physical trigger


It is important to keep in mind that some of the symptoms listed above, e.g. tiredness, disrupted sleep patterns and low sex drive, are normal after having a baby – and not necessarily indicators of PPD. If any symptoms are troubling you, try using the 
A parent with postpartum depression may also experience difficulty bonding with their baby, [11](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#fn:11 "See Footnote 11") recurrent thoughts of harming their baby, as well as recurrent thoughts of death or suicide. In severe cases, there may be suicide attempts. If a person shows signs of crisis – obvious indicators that they are strongly affected by depression or at risk of suicide – it is important to call a doctor, emergency services provider or suicide prevention line without delay.
Good to know:[12](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#fn:12 "See Footnote 12") [13](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#fn:13 "See Footnote 13") Read about different [types of depression](https://ada.com/signs-of-depression/#types).
### Postpartum depression signs in fathers
It is possible for any new parents, including dads, whether biological or adoptive, to experience postpartum depression. It is thought that as many as one in 10 new fathers may experience the condition. [14](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#fn:14 "See Footnote 14") [15](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#fn:15 "See Footnote 15")
Signs of PPD in men are largely the same as those listed above, though there may be a few differences between the sexes. For example, where women may experience sadness and seem withdrawn, their male counterparts may instead experience irritability and aggression. See this resource on [signs of depression](https://ada.com/signs-of-depression/) for more information. [14](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#fn:14 "See Footnote 14") [15](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#fn:15 "See Footnote 15")
Many men avoid seeking medical help as they may feel they are failing to fulfil parental responsibilities. However, seeing a doctor is important to manage PPD. [14](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#fn:14 "See Footnote 14") [15](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#fn:15 "See Footnote 15")
## Risk factors for postpartum depression
The causes of PPD are not fully understood. Some articles in the media suggest that postpartum depression may be caused by hormonal changes after birth, but there is not sufficient evidence to support this idea. The strongest risk factors for developing postpartum depression are thought to include: [5](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#fn:5 "See Footnote 5") [2](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2") [3](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3")
  * A personal or family history of mental health conditions, e.g. [depression](https://ada.com/conditions/depressive-episode/) or [bipolar disorder](https://ada.com/conditions/bipolar-affective-disorder/)
  * Lack of social support, i.e. friends and family
  * A poor relationship with one’s partner
  * Significant stress or major life events, e.g. death of a loved one or a major move, during or after the pregnancy


Other risk factors may include:
  * The pregnancy being unplanned
  * Being unemployed
  * Not breastfeeding
  * A complicated birth
  * The baby having health challenges or special needs
  * [Thyroid problems](https://ada.com/thyroid/) during pregnancy
  * Experiencing other health challenges during or after the pregnancy
  * One’s partner being depressed
  * Substance abuse


Good to know:[16](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#fn:16 "See Footnote 16")
## Postpartum depression diagnosis and treatment
Postpartum depression, like other types of depression, is considered a treatable condition.[depressive episodes](https://ada.com/conditions/depressive-episode/).
## Postpartum psychosis
Also known as postnatal or puerperal psychosis, this is a relatively rarePostpartum psychosis is not the same as postpartum depression.
Postpartum psychosis can be extremely serious, and is considered to be a psychiatric emergency that typically requires urgent hospital treatment.[17](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#fn:17 "See Footnote 17")
Postnatal psychosis typically develops in the first weeks after childbirth. Symptoms include: [17](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#fn:17 "See Footnote 17")
  * Unusually low mood (depression) or high mood (mania); moods may swing between the two
  * Agitation
  * Confusion
  * Sleep disturbances
  * Loss of inhibition
  * Paranoia
  * Delusions
  * Hallucinations, e.g. hearing voices
  * Loss of contact with reality


If signs of postnatal psychosis are present, emergency medical care should be sought.
Risk factors that may increase the likelihood of developing postpartum psychosis include: [17](https://ada.com/signs-of-postpartum-depression/#fn:17 "See Footnote 17")
  * A personal or family history of postpartum psychosis
  * [Bipolar disorder](https://ada.com/conditions/bipolar-affective-disorder/)
  * [Schizophrenia](https://ada.com/conditions/schizophrenia/)
  * Less commonly, severe depression

# Bakterielle Meningitis
Verfasst von [Adas medizinischem Fachpersonal](https://ada.com/de/team/medical/)
Aktualisiert am 22. Juli 2022 um 14:09 OEZ
## Auf dieser Seite
  * [Was ist eine bakterielle Meningitis?](https://ada.com/de/conditions/bacterial-meningitis/#was-ist-eine-bakterielle-meningitis)
  * [Risiken](https://ada.com/de/conditions/bacterial-meningitis/#risiken)
  * [Symptome](https://ada.com/de/conditions/bacterial-meningitis/#symptome)
  * [Diagnose](https://ada.com/de/conditions/bacterial-meningitis/#diagnose)
  * [Behandlung](https://ada.com/de/conditions/bacterial-meningitis/#behandlung)
  * [Prognose](https://ada.com/de/conditions/bacterial-meningitis/#prognose)
  * [Vorsorge](https://ada.com/de/conditions/bacterial-meningitis/#vorsorge)


* * *
Artikel teilen:
## Was ist eine bakterielle Meningitis?
Die bakterielle Meningitis ist eine bakterielle Infektion der Hirnhäute (der Membranen, die das Gehirn umgeben).
Typische Meningitis Symptome sind:
  * Kopfschmerzen,
  * ein steifer Nacken,
  * Fieber und Erbrechen.


Die Symptome können sehr plötzlich auftreten und die betroffene Person kann innerhalb weniger Stunden schwer erkranken.
Andere Bezeichnung für bakterielle Meningitis: Bakterielle Infektion der Hirn- und Rückenmarkshäute.
Finde mehr über Deine Symptome heraus.
## Risiken einer bakteriellen Meningitis
Bei Neugeborenen Kindern besteht das höchste Risiko für eine Meningitis, obwohl diese Erkrankung Menschen jeden Alters betreffen kann. Männer haben ein leicht höheres Risiko als Frauen. Für Menschen mit anderen Erkrankungen (einschließlich einer kürzlich erlittenen Ohren- oder Halsentzündung) oder Menschen, die vor kurzem eine Schädelfraktur erlitten haben, besteht ein erhöhtes Risiko einer Meningitis.
## Symptome einer bakterielle Infektion der Hirnhäute
Typische Symptome einer bakteriellen Meningitis sind:
  * Kopfschmerzen,
  * ein steifer Nacken,
  * Übelkeit,
  * Erbrechen,
  * Fieber und
  * Lichtempfindlichkeit (Photophobie).


Weitere Symptome sind unter anderem Benommenheit und Verwirrung. Manche Ursachen von Meningitis können einen dunkelvioletten, fleckigen Hautausschlag verursachen. Die Symptome können sehr plötzlich auftreten und die betroffene Person kann innerhalb weniger Stunden schwer erkranken.
Wenn Du Dir unsicher bist, ob diese Beschwerden auf Dich zutreffen, starte eine 
## Wie wird Meningitis diagnostiziert?
Die Diagnose erfolgt basierend auf den Symptomen, der körperlichen Untersuchung und Tests, welche das Vorhandensein einer schweren Infektion im Körper bestätigen. Es wird eine Probe der Rückenmarkflüssigkeit entnommen und auf die spezifischen Bakterien getestet, welche die Infektion verursachen.
## Behandlung einer bakteriellen Meningitis
Die bakterielle Meningitis ist eine ernste Erkrankung und erfordert dringend die Untersuchung durch einen Arzt. Die Infektion wird mit intravenösen Antibiotika (mittels Infusion) behandelt. Menschen mit einer bakteriellen Meningitis sind oft sehr krank und brauchen möglicherweise weitere unterstützende Maßnahmen (wie etwa Flüssigkeit zur Erhöhung des Blutdrucks), während die Antibiotika die Infektion bekämpfen.
## Prognose
Eine frühe Diagnose und Behandlung dieser Krankheit bieten die besten Chancen auf eine gute Genesung. Schwere Fälle von bakterieller Meningitis haben eine hohe Rate von Komplikationen, darunter epileptische Anfälle und Hirnschäden. Eine bakterielle Meningitis kann in einigen Fällen zum Tode führen, vor allem bei sehr jungen und älteren Erkrankten.
## Vorsorge
Einigen häufigen Ursachen einer bakteriellen Meningitis kann durch eine Impfung vorgebeugt werden. Die Einhaltung des empfohlenen Impfplans kann einigen Fällen von Meningitis vorbeugen. Eine gute Hygiene, wie etwa das Waschen der Hände, kann auch dabei helfen, einige Fälle von bakterieller Meningitis zu vermeiden.

# Pancreatic Cancer
Written by [Ada’s Medical Knowledge Team](https://ada.com/team/medical/)
Updated on February 15, 2022 at 10:00 AM GMT+2
## On this page
  * [What is pancreatic cancer?](https://ada.com/conditions/pancreatic-cancer/#what-is-pancreatic-cancer)
  * [Risks](https://ada.com/conditions/pancreatic-cancer/#risks)
  * [Symptoms](https://ada.com/conditions/pancreatic-cancer/#symptoms)
  * [Diagnosis](https://ada.com/conditions/pancreatic-cancer/#diagnosis)
  * [Treatment](https://ada.com/conditions/pancreatic-cancer/#treatment)
  * [Prevention](https://ada.com/conditions/pancreatic-cancer/#prevention)
  * [Other names for pancreatic cancer](https://ada.com/conditions/pancreatic-cancer/#other-names-for-pancreatic-cancer)


* * *
Share this article:
## What is pancreatic cancer?
Pancreatic cancer is a cancer arising from the pancreas, a digestive organ located in the upper region of the abdomen behind the stomach. This condition tends to affect older adults and people who have other medical conditions, especially pancreas conditions. Symptoms are unspecific and often occur late, which complicates diagnosis and worsens the outlook after diagnosis. It may lead to unexplained weight loss, loss of appetite, chronic back pain and pain in the upper abdomen. Diagnosis is made by MRI or CT scans. Treatment involves surgery, chemotherapy and, sometimes, radiotherapy. People who are diagnosed in the early stages have a better chance of successful treatment, but this is not common.
Feeling unwell? Get a symptom assessment with the [symptom checker](https://ada.com/app/) works before you try it for yourself.
## Risks
Cancer occurs when abnormal cells being to grow uncontrollably. These cells destroy the normal cells around them, and can spread through to other parts of the body. Pancreatic cancer involves the pancreas, an organ located in the upper region of the abdomen behind the stomach which usually produces substances which break down fats and hormones that manage blood sugar. Pancreatic cancer affects mostly people between the ages of 50 and 80, and becomes more common with age. People who smoke, who drink alcohol regularly and who are obese are at higher risk of developing pancreatic cancer. People which have another condition of the pancreas, such as diabetes, long-term inflammation (pancreatitis) or pancreatic cysts also tend to develop pancreas cancer more commonly. In some cases, pancreas cancer tends to run in families, and some genes and specific hereditary conditions are known to increase the risk of developing pancreatic cancer, such as Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.
## Symptoms
There are often no symptoms in the early stages of pancreatic cancer. The most common symptoms of pancreas cancer include [abdominal pain which spreads to the back](https://ada.com/conditions/abdominal-pain/), unexplained weight loss and yellowing of the skin and eyes. Other symptoms commonly include nausea, loss of appetite and constipation. Many people find that their stools change color or consistency and appear paler and greasier than previously. Rarer symptoms include blood sugar problems and recurrent blood clots in the veins.
## Diagnosis
Diagnosis is based on the symptoms and a physical examination of the skin and abdomen which may reveal yellowing of the skin and an enlarged gallbladder. Some people are diagnosed during investigation for a cause of changes in their blood sugar levels. An ultrasound, CT scan or MRI scan of the abdomen is done to confirm the diagnosis, and a small sample of the pancreas (a biopsy) will be taken and investigated for cancer.
## Treatment
Treatment depends on the size, specific type of cancer and whether the cancer has a spread at the time of diagnosis. These factors are used to determine the stage of the cancer. The treatment involves surgery, chemotherapy or radiotherapy, or most commonly, a combination of these. The treating doctor can give the best advice in individual cases. Emotional counseling or joining a support group may also be helpful. People who have pancreatic cancer which cannot be cured may receive treatments which aim to improve their symptoms and quality of life.
## Prevention
Reducing alcohol intake and giving up smoking can help to reduce the risk of developing pancreas cancer. Maintaining good health, including maintaining a healthy weight and taking care to manage other health problems, such as diabetes, may also be helpful.
## Other names for pancreatic cancer
  * Malignant neoplasm of pancreas

# Managing a healthy pregnancy
[Dr. Kini](https://ada.com/editorial/writers/dr-nisha-kini/)
Medically reviewed
Updated on April 8, 2025 at 3:00 PM GMT+2
Pregnancy can be an exciting but stressful time. As you get ready to welcome a new person into the world, your body will undergo big changes, both visible and invisible. 
Understandably, you’re going to have questions about how to keep you and your baby safe and healthy.
To help you, I’ve picked out the 3 things people ask me about most when they get pregnant: [pregnancy](https://ada.com/conditions/pregnancy/). 
Are you looking for advice on how to manage a healthy pregnancy? Ada is a free medical app that can help you understand your symptoms and manage your health 24/7. 
## 1. Staying active
The first question most newly pregnant people ask me is ‘Can I carry on exercising?’ The answer is not that you can, but that you should. 
Here are some of the benefits of staying active while pregnant:
  * Reduced cesarean section rates[1](https://ada.com/editorial/managing-a-healthy-pregnancy/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1")
  * Healthier weight gain[1](https://ada.com/editorial/managing-a-healthy-pregnancy/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1")
  * Improved management of gestational diabetes[1](https://ada.com/editorial/managing-a-healthy-pregnancy/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1")
  * Reduced constipation[2](https://ada.com/editorial/managing-a-healthy-pregnancy/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2")
  * Shortened labor[3](https://ada.com/editorial/managing-a-healthy-pregnancy/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3")


Exercising during [pregnancy](https://ada.com/conditions/pregnancy/) could also be good for your baby. Studies link healthy body weight, cardiovascular health, and nervous system development in children to staying active while pregnant.[4](https://ada.com/editorial/managing-a-healthy-pregnancy/#fn:4 "See Footnote 4")
So what sort of exercise should you be doing? Aim for 2.5 hours of moderate aerobic activity a week. Walking, swimming, yoga, and strength training are all safe, but speak to your doctor before starting a new exercise program.
Whatever exercise you choose, go gently. A good rule of thumb is to make sure you can still carry a conversation while exercising.
Here are some things to avoid when you’re exercising during pregnancy:[5](https://ada.com/editorial/managing-a-healthy-pregnancy/#fn:5 "See Footnote 5")
  * Any activity where there’s a risk of direct impact to your belly
  * Exercise in hot weather
  * Lying on your back for too long, especially after 16 weeks


## 2. Diet
The second question people ask is usually about what to eat during pregnancy. Unfortunately, it isn’t easy to give a one-size-fits-all answer because there are so many different healthy diets.
My advice is to continue eating a balanced diet of proteins, carbohydrates, and fats. And, of course, plenty of fruit and vegetables. Your calorie intake will need to increase as your fetus starts to grow. Speak to your doctor about the right amount of calories for your body type at your stage of pregnancy. 
There are a few things you should try to avoid while pregnant:[6](https://ada.com/editorial/managing-a-healthy-pregnancy/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6")
  * Unpasteurized milk
  * Soft cheeses and blue cheeses
  * Raw or undercooked meat
  * Raw eggs
  * Fish with high mercury content
  * Organ meat like liver, heart, and kidney
  * Unwashed fruit and vegetables
  * Alcohol
  * Multivitamins and supplements containing vitamin A


Speak to your doctor before you start taking any supplements while pregnant.
## 3. Managing common health complaints
Most pregnancies follow a healthy course without too many problems. However, you can expect to experience some health changes. Here are some ways to manage the most common ones.
### Morning sickness
Experiencing a bit of morning sickness during your first trimester is normal. It should stop around weeks 16-20.[7](https://ada.com/editorial/managing-a-healthy-pregnancy/#fn:7 "See Footnote 7") Try eating small meals more often, and avoid foods that are more likely to give you an upset stomach. If your morning sickness doesn’t go away or you’re struggling to keep food down, call your doctor. 
### Constipation
Constipation during pregnancy can be uncomfortable, but it’s normal.[7](https://ada.com/editorial/managing-a-healthy-pregnancy/#fn:7 "See Footnote 7") Drinking plenty of water, eating lots of fiber, and making sure you stay active will help you stay regular. Talk to your doctor before taking laxatives.
### Tiredness
Being pregnant can be exhausting work. You’re growing a new human after all. Try to get as much sleep as possible, and take naps in the day if you need to. Avoid taking any over-the-counter medications to help you sleep. Speak to your doctor if fatigue becomes a serious problem for you.
I hope these tips will help you on your way to managing a healthy pregnancy. Until next time, take care of yourself.
You can start making better health choices now by

# Chronic migraines
Written by [Ada’s Medical Knowledge Team](https://ada.com/team/medical/)
Updated on October 23, 2024 at 10:40 AM GMT+3
## On this page
  * [Overview](https://ada.com/conditions/chronic-migraines/#overview)
  * [What is chronic migraine? ](https://ada.com/conditions/chronic-migraines/#what-is-chronic-migraine)
  * [Symptoms](https://ada.com/conditions/chronic-migraines/#symptoms)
  * [Causes](https://ada.com/conditions/chronic-migraines/#causes)
  * [How long do chronic migraines last?](https://ada.com/conditions/chronic-migraines/#how-long-do-chronic-migraines-last)
  * [Diagnosis](https://ada.com/conditions/chronic-migraines/#diagnosis)
  * [Treatments](https://ada.com/conditions/chronic-migraines/#treatments)
  * [Wrapping up](https://ada.com/conditions/chronic-migraines/#wrapping-up)
  * [FAQs](https://ada.com/conditions/chronic-migraines/#faqs)


* * *
Share this article:
## Overview
  * Chronic migraine is a form of migraine which causes headaches for more than 15 days per month
  * Chronic migraine usually occurs in people who already had episodes of migraine in the past
  * Chronic migraine treatment focuses on prevention and relieving symptoms 


Think you might be experiencing chronicmigraine
Chronic migraine is a type of migraine that lasts for a longer period of time
## What is chronic migraine? 
Chronic migraine[type of migraine](https://ada.com/conditions/migraine-headache/#types-of-migraines) that lasts for a longer period of time. It is characterized by experiencing headaches for at least 15 days per month[1](https://ada.com/conditions/chronic-migraines/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1")
## What are possible chronic migraine symptoms?
The symptoms of chronic migraine are the same as with regular migraine, with the exception that they occur much more frequently.
The most common symptoms of a chronic migraine [2](https://ada.com/conditions/chronic-migraines/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2")
  * Throbbing, pulsating pain on one side of the head. This pain may affect the eye area but can occur anywhere in the head or the neck.
  * Sensitivity to light, sound, and/or smell
  * Vision changes
  * Nausea
  * Vomiting


Besides these common symptoms of a migraine, it’s also possible to experience
  * Loss of appetite 
  * Muscle tenderness 
  * Impaired concentration 
  * Fatigue
  * Anxiety
  * Other symptoms


## What causes chronic migraines?
Chronic migraine causes are not yet fully understood by scientists. It often appears in people who have already experienced episodes of migraine in the past. A number of conditions can increase your risk of getting a migraine[1](https://ada.com/conditions/chronic-migraines/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1")
  * Anxiety
  * [Depression](https://ada.com/conditions/depressive-episode/)
  * [Fibromyalgia](https://ada.com/conditions/fibromyalgia/)
  * [Sleep apnea](https://ada.com/conditions/sleep-apnea/)
  * Postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome


It’s important to know that the misuse of migraine medication may lead to daily migraine as well[1](https://ada.com/conditions/chronic-migraines/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1")
## How long do chronic migraines last?
Chronic migraine lasts for three months and upwards[1](https://ada.com/conditions/chronic-migraines/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1")
## How can chronic migraine be diagnosed?
To diagnose chronic migraine, your physician will ask you questions about the symptomsheadache diary
Apart from the questions your physician may ask you, there is no specific test to diagnose chronic migraine. Your physician may perform a neurological examination or run additional tests in order to rule out other conditions that may be the cause of your headache.
Think you might be experiencing chronicmigraine
## Which options exist for chronic migraine treatment?
Daily migraines can be treated in various ways. The best form of treatment is a preventative treatment, which aims at relieving your symptoms and reducing the amount of days that you experience headaches. Prevention for chronic migraine can take on many forms: [1](https://ada.com/conditions/chronic-migraines/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [4](https://ada.com/conditions/chronic-migraines/#fn:4 "See Footnote 4") [5](https://ada.com/conditions/chronic-migraines/#fn:5 "See Footnote 5")
  1. Preventive chronic migraine medication
  2. Botox 
  3. Calcitonin gene-related peptide monoclonal antibodies
  4. Greater occipital nerve block


In moments when you can feel that your chronic migraine is getting worse, you could opt for over-the-counter painkillers and triptans[2](https://ada.com/conditions/chronic-migraines/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2")
Consistent migraines can also be improved by making lifestyle alterations. You may benefit from:
  * Developing techniques to manage and reduce stress
  * Keeping a diary to identify migraine triggers
  * Sleeping well, and establishing a consistent sleep cycle
  * Staying hydrated
  * Establishing regular meal times, and adopting a healthy, balanced diet
  * Devising a new medication plan 


Following a safe weight-loss program
## Wrapping up
Chronic migraine can cause headaches for more than 15 days per month, out of which 8 of those days you can also experience additional symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, and vision changes. Treatment can vary, but most often it’s a combination of lifestyle alterations and preventative medication that can decrease the frequency and severity of your headaches. 
## Find out more about your symptoms
## Chronic migraine FAQs
Q: Why do I keep getting migraines every day?   
A: Getting migraines every day can be a symptom of chronic migraine. This is a type of migraine in which you can experience migraine headaches over 15 days per month, often combined with other migraine symptoms.
Q: Is chronic migraine a disability?   
A: Chronic migraine is a valid reason to apply for disability, as its symptoms can have a severe impact on your daily activities and quality of life. 
Q: Can you get rid of chronic migraines?   
A: In about 20% of people, chronic migraines go away on their own within 2 years. Others may continue to experience symptoms. There are however treatment options available to relieve your symptoms and the intensity of the headaches you’re experiencing. 
Q: What causes chronic migraines?   
A: The exact cause of chronic migraines is not known. There are however some conditions such as anxiety, depression, and fibromyalgia which may contribute to the development of chronic migraines.

# Meningite viral
Escrito pelo nosso [Medical Knowledge Team](https://ada.com/pt/team/medical/)
Atualizado em 15 de fevereiro de 2022 às 10:00 GMT+2
## Nesta página
  * [Visão geral](https://ada.com/pt/conditions/viral-meningitis/#visao-geral)
  * [Riscos](https://ada.com/pt/conditions/viral-meningitis/#riscos)
  * [Sintomas](https://ada.com/pt/conditions/viral-meningitis/#sintomas)

Compartilhe esse artigo:
## Visão geral
meningite viral é uma infecção virai das meninges (as membranas que envolvem o cérebro e medula espinal). Há muitos vírus que podem causar esta infecção e muitos destes vírus são muito comuns. A meningite viral é mais comum em recém-nascidos e crianças pequenas. Os sintomas da meningite viral incluem dor de cabeça, náuseas, vômitos, irritabilidade, perda de apetite e sonolência. Embora as crianças mais velhas e adultos muitas vezes não necessitem nenhum tratamento específico para a meningite viral, recém-nascidos e crianças pequenas podem precisar de medicamentos anti-virais. Os recém-nascidos e crianças têm um risco maior de complicações após um episódio de meningite viral. Vacinações e boa higiene podem ajudar a prevenir alguns casos de meningite viral.
Você se preocupa que você ou um familiar seu possam ter essa condição? Comece sua [o aplicativo](https://ada.com/pt/app/) primeiro.
## Riscos
A meningite viral é a causa mais comum de meningite. Ela afeta mais comumente recém-nascidos, lactentes e crianças, embora possa afetar pessoas de qualquer idade. Muitos vírus comuns podem causar meningite viral, incluindo o virus da gripe, vírus da herpes e da doença mão-pé-boca. Causas virais menos comuns são papeira, sarampo, o vírus da imunodeficiência humana (HIV), vírus da poliomielite e vírus do Nilo Ocidental, embora existam muitos mais. As crianças que não cumpriram inteiramente o programa de vacinas podem estar em maior risco de meningite viral. Recém-nascidos e crianças que estão em contato com pessoas com infecções virais também estão em maior risco de ter esta condição.
## Sintomas
Os sintomas típicos desta doença incluem dor de cabeça, rigidez de nuca, febre, náuseas e vômitos. Os recém-nascidos e bebês podem ter perda de apetite, podem chorar ou ficar anormalmente irritáveis ou sonolentos. As infecções virais também podem causar sintomas de infecção em outras partes do corpo ao mesmo tempo, como uma erupção cutânea ou falta de ar.
## Diagnóstico
O diagnóstico é baseado nos sintomas, exame clíico e testes de uma amostra de líquido cefalorraquidiano (o fluido nas meninges ao redor do cérebro e da coluna) para sinais de meningite nas meninges e para excluir a possibilidade de uma infecção bacteriana. Este exame também é utilizado para identificar o vírus específico que causa a infecção.
## Tratamento
Em crianças mais velhas e adultos, nenhum tratamento específico é necessário na maioria dos casos. Essas pessoas devem ter um tratamento para seus sintomas. Acetaminofeno (paracetamol) pode ser útil para tratar dores de cabeça, e essas pessoas também devem tomar bastante líquido. Recém-nascidos e crianças pequenas, ou pessoas com sinais de complicação, pode exigir medicação anti-viral para combater o vírus que causa a infecção.
## Prevenção
Algumas causas comuns de meningite viral são evitáveis através de vacinação. Cumprindo o esquema de vacinação recomendado pode ajudar a prevenir alguns casos de meningite. Uma boa higiene, tal como lavar as mãos, também pode ajudar a evitar a meningite viral.
## Prognóstico
Os recém-nascidos estão em maior risco de ter complicações após um episódio de meningite viral, e podem sofrer graves consequências, como inchaço no cérebro, dificuldades de aprendizagem, surdez ou convulsões. Nesta faixa etária, a meningite viral pode ser fatal. As crianças mais velhas e adultos geralmente começam a se sentir melhor dentro de 7 a 10 dias após ter tido meningite viral, e se recuperam bem. A recuperação total pode levar semanas. Nessa faixa etária é raro desenvolver complicações de longa duração depois de ter tido meningite viral .
## Outros nomes
  * infecção viral ao redor do cérebro e da medula espinhal

## What is celiac disease?
Celiac disease is a serious, lifelong condition caused by the immune system reacting to gluten,[1](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [2](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2")
Symptoms of celiac disease in adults and children may include: [1](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [3](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3")
  * [Abdominal (belly) pain or discomfort](https://ada.com/conditions/abdominal-pain/)
  * Diarrhea
  * Fatty, pale, smelly stools that float in the toilet
  * Rash
  * Fatigue
  * Irritability and [depression](https://ada.com/signs-of-depression/)


However, many people have no symptoms or only mild symptoms, which can make a timely diagnosis challenging. Celiac disease often goes unrecognized;[2](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2")
Celiac disease can affect anyone, of any age, though it tends to be more common among women than men. It occurs in approximately one out of every 100 people. There seem to be two peak periods in the appearance of symptoms – one in the first year of life, between eight and 12 months of age, and the second between approximately 20-40 years of age. Celiac disease is linked to certain genes and is often found to run in families. [1](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [3](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3") [6](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:6 "See Footnote 6")
In people with celiac disease, eating food that contains gluten causes a severe response from the immune system; it mistakenly damages the lining of the small intestine, leading to difficulty absorbing nutrients and a number of potential complications. [1](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [2](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2")
There is currently no cure or way to prevent celiac disease. The only treatment for celiac disease is a lifelong gluten-free diet.[1](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [3](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3") [2](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2")
Think you might be experiencing celiac disease
## Celiac disease symptoms
The symptoms of celiac disease can vary widely and range from mild to severe. If present, they are typically persistent.
Gastrointestinal (digestive tract) symptoms in adults may include: [1](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [3](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3") [7](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:7 "See Footnote 7")
  * Transient abdominal (belly) pain
  * Bloating
  * Flatulence or excess wind
  * Fatty, pale, smelly stools that float in the toilet
  * Diarrhea or, rarely, constipation
  * Poor appetite
  * Nausea and vomiting


Other signs and symptoms of celiac disease in adults may include: [1](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [8](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:8 "See Footnote 8") [7](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:7 "See Footnote 7")
  * Fatigue and lethargy
  * [Anemia](https://ada.com/conditions/anemia/)
  * Severe or persistent [mouth ulcers](https://ada.com/conditions/aphthous-ulcers/), or canker sores
  * Dermatitis herpetiformis, a type of rash
  * Unintentional weight loss
  * Lack of menstruation
  * Infertility
  * Repeated [miscarriage](https://ada.com/conditions/miscarriage/)
  * [Osteoporosis](https://ada.com/conditions/osteoporosis/)
  * Unexplained bone or joint pain
  * Dental enamel problems
  * Ataxia, loss of coordination
  * Peripheral neuropathy; tingling, numbness or pain in the hands and feet
  * [Headaches](https://ada.com/conditions/headache/)
  * Irritability
  * [Depression](https://ada.com/conditions/depressive-episode/) or [anxiety](https://ada.com/conditions/generalized-anxiety-disorder/)
  * Dementia, in older people


Many adults with celiac disease do not have any symptoms, or only have mild symptoms.
## Causes of celiac disease
Celiac disease is caused by a severe response to gluten,[1](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") It is not understood exactly why this happens. [9](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:9 "See Footnote 9")
Reacting to gluten, the immune system causes inflammation and irritation in the lining of the small intestine.[1](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [3](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3") [2](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2")
### Risk factors for celiac disease
Celiac disease can affect anyone, of any age and racial background. However, certain factors may make a person more likely to develop celiac disease. These include: [1](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [8](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:8 "See Footnote 8")
  * Having a close relative, e.g. a parent or sibling, with celiac disease; this significantly increases one’s risk
  * Having another autoimmune condition, e.g. [Hashimoto’s thyroiditis](https://ada.com/conditions/hashimotos-thyroiditis-hypothyroidism/), [type 1 diabetes](https://ada.com/conditions/diabetes/#types) or [rheumatoid arthritis](https://ada.com/conditions/rheumatoid-arthritis/)
  * Turner syndrome, a disorder in which a female only has one out of two X chromosomes
  * Down syndrome, also known as trisomy 21


Think you might be experiencing celiac disease
### Celiac disease and “leaky gut”
The terms “leaky gut” and “leaky gut syndrome” are often encountered by people looking for information on celiac disease and/or gluten sensitivity. Leaky gut and leaky gut syndrome are not recognized medical terms.[10](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:10 "See Footnote 10") [11](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:11 "See Footnote 11") [13](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:13 "See Footnote 13")
In a healthy intestine, the gaps between cells in the mucosal barrier are usually very small, only allowing appropriately digested nutrients and other substances through to the bloodstream. However, certain substances and conditions can cause the gaps to widen or the intestinal barrier to become “loose” or “leaky”. Celiac disease is one such condition. It is thought that gluten may cause increased intestinal permeability in a number of people without celiac disease, too. [10](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:10 "See Footnote 10") [11](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:11 "See Footnote 11") [13](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:13 "See Footnote 13")
There is a theory that increased intestinal permeability might allow potentially harmful substances, e.g. undigested proteins, bacteria and toxins, to pass from the gut into the bloodstream and cause widespread inflammation in the body, with a range of resulting health problems. [10](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:10 "See Footnote 10") [11](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:11 "See Footnote 11") [13](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:13 "See Footnote 13")
There is not enough evidence to confirm many of the ideas about leaky gut and the possible effects it may have in the body.[10](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:10 "See Footnote 10") [11](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:11 "See Footnote 11")
If you have any questions about your digestive health, it is recommended that you consult a medical doctor.
## Diagnosis of celiac disease
After taking the person’s medical history and performing a physical examination, a doctor will typically order [blood tests](https://ada.com/blood-test-results/) if celiac disease is suspected. If the results suggest that celiac disease is present, a biopsy will then be recommended to confirm the diagnosis. [1](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1")
Good to know:do not go gluten-free until you have spoken to a doctor and been tested,[1](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [9](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:9 "See Footnote 9")
### Celiac disease blood test
A blood test is used to check for the antibodies, proteins that typically fight infection and which are typical of celiac disease. These include IgA tissue transglutaminase (IgA tTG), endomysial IgA and IgG deamidated gliadin peptide. The levels of these antibodies are usually only high in people with celiac disease. [9](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:9 "See Footnote 9") A doctor may also recommend blood tests to check for nutritional deficiencies, e.g. iron deficiency. [1](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1")
### Celiac disease biopsy
If the blood test shows high levels of the antibodies found in celiac disease, a diagnosis will typically need to be confirmed with a biopsy of the duodenum, the first part of the small intestine. This involves a doctor taking a small sample of tissue, typically using an endoscope – a thin tube that is passed down the throat into the stomach and intestine. The sample is examined for signs of the characteristic damage caused by celiac disease. [1](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [9](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:9 "See Footnote 9")
### Genetic test for celiac disease
In some cases, it may be possible to have a test to check for the presence of the genes that are associated with celiac disease. Not having HLA-DQ2 or HLA-DQ8 genes means that developing celiac disease is highly unlikely. However, having the genes does not mean that a person will develop celiac disease; the majority of people with a genetic predisposition to celiac disease never develop the condition.[14](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:14 "See Footnote 14") [15](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:15 "See Footnote 15")
## Celiac disease treatment
There is currently no cure for celiac disease – treatment requires adopting a completely gluten-free diet. In addition, certain supplements and vaccinations may be recommended to help prevent complications from celiac disease. [1](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1")
### Gluten-free diet
The only effective treatment for celiac disease is a diet that is 100 percent free of gluten.[1](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [3](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3") [2](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2")
A strict gluten-free diet must be followed for life; the consumption of even a very small amount of gluten can cause damage to the small intestine and trigger a relapse of symptoms.[1](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1")
Gluten is found in the following grains: [1](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [3](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3")
  * Wheat
  * Rye
  * Barley
  * Spelt
  * Einkorn
  * Kamut
  * Triticale


Any foods that contain the above, e.g. breads, pastries and many cereals, will therefore also contain gluten, and must be avoided. Sauces, snack foods, ready-made meals, beers and even medicines are among the many products that often contain gluten; labels should always be checked carefully.
Gluten is not found in the following unprocessed starches:
  * Rice
  * Potatoes
  * Corn


#### Oats and celiac disease
There are differing opinions on whether oats are suitable for people with celiac disease. Oats contain a protein called avenin, which is similar to gluten. For some people with celiac disease, this does not seem to be a problem. However, others find that it causes a relapse of symptoms and/or damage to the small intestine. Furthermore, some brands of oats may be contaminated with gluten from the factories they are processed in. Some celiac disease authorities advise that oats be included in a person’s diet, while others recommend avoiding all oats and oat products. A doctor may be able to advise on what is most appropriate for a particular person’s dietary needs. [16](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:16 "See Footnote 16") [8](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:8 "See Footnote 8") [17](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:17 "See Footnote 17") [18](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:18 "See Footnote 18")
Good to know:
### Other measures
A doctor may recommend the following measures to help prevent nutritional deficiencies and other complications from celiac disease: [1](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [19](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:19 "See Footnote 19")
  * Taking a vitamin, calcium or iron supplement, for at least six months after diagnosis
  * Having the seasonal “flu jab”, the yearly [influenza](https://ada.com/conditions/influenza-infection/) vaccination
  * Having other vaccinations, e.g. the Hib vaccine to prevent [blood poisoning](https://ada.com/conditions/sepsis/) and [pneumonia](https://ada.com/conditions/pneumonia/), and the pneumococcal vaccine [20](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:20 "See Footnote 20")


## Complications of celiac disease
Maintaining a strictly gluten-free diet is essential to prevent symptoms and lower the likelihood of complications from celiac disease. Eating even a tiny amount of gluten can cause symptoms and increase the risk of developing complications.[1](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1")
Complications associated with poorly managed celiac disease include: [1](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [9](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:9 "See Footnote 9")
  * [Vitamin D deficiency](https://ada.com/conditions/vitamin-d-deficiency/), [iron deficiency](https://ada.com/conditions/iron-deficiency-anemia/) and other nutrient deficiencies
  * [Osteoporosis](https://ada.com/conditions/osteoporosis/)
  * Skin problems, e.g. dermatitis herpetiformis
  * Ulcers in the intestine, known as ulcerative jejunitis
  * Weakened functioning of the spleen and possibly the immune system as a result [20](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:20 "See Footnote 20")
  * Other autoimmune conditions, e.g. [type 1 diabetes](https://ada.com/conditions/diabetes/#types) and [Hashimoto’s thyroiditis](https://ada.com/conditions/hashimotos-thyroiditis-hypothyroidism/)
  * [Anxiety](https://ada.com/conditions/generalized-anxiety-disorder/) and [depression](https://ada.com/conditions/depressive-episode/)
  * Rarely, lymphoma, a cancer of the intestinal lymph system, and other cancers of the gastrointestinal tract [21](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:21 "See Footnote 21")
  * Infertility
  * In undiagnosed women having a child, low birth weight, premature birth or [miscarriage](https://ada.com/conditions/miscarriage/)
  * In children, stunted growth, delayed puberty and dental problems


### Non-responsive celiac disease
About one in 10 people with celiac disease will continue to experience symptoms after they have switched to a strict gluten-free diet. This is often caused by hidden sources of gluten in the diet, but may also be the result of: [9](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:9 "See Footnote 9")
  * Food intolerances, e.g. lactose, a sugar found in cow’s milk
  * Food allergies
  * Bacterial overgrowth in the small intestine
  * [Irritable bowel syndrome](https://ada.com/conditions/irritable-bowel-syndrome/)
  * Microscopic colitis
  * A deficiency of pancreatic enzymes
  * Refractory celiac disease


### Refractory celiac disease
A small number of people with celiac disease may continue to experience gastrointestinal symptoms even on a confirmed gluten-free diet, or experience short-term relief when going gluten-free and then a recurrence of symptoms. This is called refractory celiac disease. The cause is unknown, and the condition requires treatment with immunosuppressive medication, e.g. steroids. [9](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:9 "See Footnote 9")
## Prevention of celiac disease
Previously, it was thought, by not introducing gluten into a baby’s diet until they were 4-6 months old, it might be possible to prevent or slow the development of celiac disease. However, recent research shows that the period at which gluten is first introduced does not affect the development of the condition. It is not yet possible to prevent celiac disease in children or adults.[22](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:22 "See Footnote 22")
Nonetheless, early diagnosis and treatment can help to prevent further development of, and complications from, celiac disease.
## Celiac disease in children
Celiac disease can affect people of any age, including infants and children. If present, symptoms of celiac disease in children are typically persistent.
Gastrointestinal (digestive tract) symptoms in children may include: [24](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:24 "See Footnote 24") [25](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:25 "See Footnote 25")
  * Diarrhea or constipation
  * Fatty, pale and smelly [1](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") stools that float in the toilet
  * Bloating or abdominal (belly) pain
  * Flatulence, commonly known as gas
  * Weak appetite
  * Nausea and vomiting [1](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1")


Other signs and symptoms in children may include: [24](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:24 "See Footnote 24") [25](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:25 "See Footnote 25")
  * Fatigue
  * [Anemia](https://ada.com/conditions/anemia/)
  * Unexplained weight loss or difficulty gaining weight
  * Delayed growth and/or puberty
  * Severe or persistent [mouth ulcers](https://ada.com/conditions/aphthous-ulcers/), or canker sores
  * Dermatitis herpetiformis, a type of rash
  * Dental problems, e.g. discolored teeth or grooves in the teeth
  * Thinning of the bones
  * Anxiety and/or irritability [26](https://ada.com/conditions/coeliac-disease/#fn:26 "See Footnote 26")
  * Sleep disturbances


Many children with celiac disease do not have any symptoms, or only have mild symptoms.
If a child is suspected of having celiac disease, a doctor will typically recommend blood tests before making any dietary changes
Treatment for celiac disease in babies and children is the same for adults and requires a strictly gluten-free diet. While this may be challenging for the family, it is necessary at all times, without exception and must be continued for the rest of the person’s life to avoid complications. Support groups are available to assist families in adjusting to and managing a 100 percent gluten-free lifestyle.
## Other names for celiac disease
  * Coeliac disease (UK spelling)
  * Celiac sprue
  * Non-tropical sprue
  * Gluten-sensitive enteropathy
  * Gluten intolerance (however, celiac disease is more serious than the mild sensitivity to gluten experienced by many people)

# Infecção do trato urinário
Escrito pelo nosso [Medical Knowledge Team](https://ada.com/pt/team/medical/)
Atualizado em 15 de março de 2022 às 18:23 GMT+2
## Nesta página
  * [Visão geral](https://ada.com/pt/conditions/urinary-tract-infection/#visao-geral)
  * [Riscos](https://ada.com/pt/conditions/urinary-tract-infection/#riscos)
  * [Sintomas](https://ada.com/pt/conditions/urinary-tract-infection/#sintomas)
  * [Diagnóstico](https://ada.com/pt/conditions/urinary-tract-infection/#diagnostico)
  * [Tratamento](https://ada.com/pt/conditions/urinary-tract-infection/#tratamento)
  * [Prevenção](https://ada.com/pt/conditions/urinary-tract-infection/#prevencao)
  * [Prognóstico](https://ada.com/pt/conditions/urinary-tract-infection/#prognostico)


* * *
Compartilhe esse artigo:
## Visão geral
infecção do trato urinário é uma infecção do sistema urinário, causada pela bactérias infectando qualquer parte do sistema urinário. O sistema urinário inclui a uretra (o tubo entre a bexiga e a pele), a bexiga, os ureteres (tubos entre os rins e da bexiga) e os rins. Infecção da bexiga é chamada de cistite. Infecção dos rins é chamado de pielonefrite. A infecção é não-transmissível. Em geral ela ocorre quando bactérias do intestino ou a região genital sobem através da uretra para a bexiga ou rim. Os sintomas incluem febre, dor na parte inferior do abdômen, micção frequente mas urinando pequenas porções e um cheiro estranho na urina. Com o tratamento com antibiótico, a maioria das pessoas se recupera rapidamente.
## Riscos
As mulheres são mais propensas à infecção uma vez que a sua uretra (o tubo entre a bexiga e da pele) é mais curta. Mulheres em pós-menopausa podem ser mais suscetíveis a essa condição do que as mulheres na pré-menopausa. Qualquer obstrução que prejudica o fluxo de urina aumenta o risco de infecção do trato urinário, por exemplo, aumento da próstata ou pedras nos rins. Outros fatores de risco incluem um sistema imunitário enfraquecido, a gravidez, uso de cateteres urinários e diabetes.
## Sintomas
A infecção do trato urinário inferior afeta a bexiga e produz sintomas como micção dolorosa e frequente, dor na parte de baixo da barriga e urina de cheiro forte, por vezes com sangue e turva. Outros sintomas podem incluir febre, calafrios e sensação geral de mal estar. Uma dor nos flancos ou nas costas pode ser um sinal de que a infecção se espalhou para os rins ([pielonefrite](https://ada.com/pt/conditions/acute-pyelonephritis/)).
Você se preocupa que você ou um familiar seu possam ter essa condição? Comece sua [o aplicativo](https://ada.com/pt/app/) primeiro.
## Diagnóstico
O diagnóstico é baseado nos sintomas e no exame físico e confirmado por um exame de urina, que testa para presença de sangue e pus. Pode ser necessário enviar a urina para um laboratório para diagnosticar as bactérias específicas que causam a infecção. Também pode ser necessário fazer uma ecografia da bexiga e rins, se a pessoa sofre de infecções urinárias recorrentes.
## Tratamento
Infecções do trato urinário são tratadas com antibióticos. Uma boa hidratação ajuda a expulsar as bactérias para fora da bexiga. Em casos de pielonefrite (infecção dos rins), repouso é recomendado. Se a causa subjacente é uma malformação do trato urinário ou obstrução da bexiga, poderá ser necessária terapia adicional.
## Prevenção
Manter a área do meato urinário (onde a urina sai do corpo) limpa ajuda a evitar infecções do trato urinário. Evitar métodos contraceptivos que contêm espermicida pode ser útil para evitar infecções do trato urinário. Esvaziar a bexiga após a relação sexual pode ajudar a prevenir infecções em mulheres. Em alguns casos em que existem infecções do trato urinário recorrentes, devem ser considerada a profilaxia com antibióticos .
## Prognóstico
Com o tratamento antibiótico adequado, a cistite (infecção da bexiga) geralmente melhora dentro de alguns dias, sem quaisquer complicações. A pielonefrite (infecção dos rins) geralmente leva mais tempo para sarar, e pode causar cicatrização nos rins. Infecções do trato urinário podem tornar-se recorrentes, especialmente em pessoas com outras condições médicas.
## Saiba mais sobre seus sintomas

# Rheumatisches Fieber
Verfasst von [Adas medizinischem Fachpersonal](https://ada.com/de/team/medical/)
Aktualisiert am 14. Juli 2022 um 08:05 OEZ
## Auf dieser Seite
  * [Was ist rheumatisches Fieber?](https://ada.com/de/conditions/rheumatic-fever/#was-ist-rheumatisches-fieber)
  * [Risiken](https://ada.com/de/conditions/rheumatic-fever/#risiken)
  * [Symptome](https://ada.com/de/conditions/rheumatic-fever/#symptome)
  * [Diagnose](https://ada.com/de/conditions/rheumatic-fever/#diagnose)
  * [Behandlung](https://ada.com/de/conditions/rheumatic-fever/#behandlung)

  * [Vorsorge](https://ada.com/de/conditions/rheumatic-fever/#vorsorge)

Artikel teilen:
## Was ist rheumatisches Fieber?
Das rheumatische Fieber ist eine entzündliche Erkrankung, die nach einer Mandelentzündung auftritt. Es wird durch spezifische Bakterien (Streptokokken der Gruppe A) verursacht und betrifft meist die Gelenke und das Herz.
Es kann viele verschiedene Symptome auslösen, die häufigsten sind jedoch Fieber sowie Schmerzen und Schwellungen der Gelenke. Andere Beschwerden sind:
  * Brustschmerzen,
  * Husten,
  * Atemnot,
  * ungewollte Bewegungen (Chorea) und ein
  * Hautausschlag.


Das rheumatische Fieber wird mit Antibiotika behandelt. Manche Kinder mit rheumatischem Fieber können Herzklappenprobleme entwickeln.
Finde mehr über Deine Symptome heraus.
## Risiken
Das rheumatische Fieber ist in vielen Ländern selten geworden, da die zugrunde liegende Krankheit, eine bakterielle Infektion der Mandeln, mit Antibiotika behandelt werden kann.
Dennoch kommt es häufig in Teilen der Welt vor, in denen es keinen Zugang zu medizinischer Versorgung gibt und enge Platzverhältnisse herrschen. Diese Erkrankung kommt häufig bei Kindern im Alter zwischen fünf und 15 Jahren vor. Erwachsene erkranken selten daran. Kinder, die bei einer [bakteriellen Mandelentzündung](https://ada.com/de/conditions/tonsillitis/) nicht umgehend behandelt werden, haben ein erhöhtes Risiko für diese Erkrankung.
## Symptome
Symptome entwickeln sich innerhalb von zehn bis 20 Tagen nach einer bakteriellen Infektion der Mandeln oder des Rachens.
Sie umfassen:
  * Fieber,
  * Kopfschmerzen,
  * Schwäche,
  * einen nicht juckenden Hautausschlag und
  * Gelenkschmerzen, die meist die großen Gelenke betreffen und sich von einem Gelenk auf das andere ausbreiten.


Später können ungewollte Muskelbewegungen auftreten. Manche Menschen entwickeln möglicherweise eine [Karditis (Herzmuskelentzündung)](https://ada.com/de/conditions/myocarditis/), die Brustschmerzen, Husten und Atemnot verursacht.
## Diagnose
Die Diagnose erfolgt basierend auf den Symptomen und einer körperlichen Untersuchung. Sie wird durch Blutuntersuchungen, die Hinweise auf das Vorliegen einer Entzündung geben, unterstützt. Darüber hinaus kann eine Untersuchung des Herzens mittels eines Elektrokardiogramms (EKG) und einer Ultraschalluntersuchung erforderlich sein.
## Behandlung
Die bakterielle Infektion wird mit Antibiotikaentzündungshemmende Medikamente
## Prognose
Die Prognose nach einem rheumatischen Fieber hängt davon ab, ob das Herz betroffen ist. Viele Kinder erholen sich gut und haben keine Komplikationen. Einige Betroffene benötigen dauerhaft Antibiotika, um eine erneute Infektion zu verhindern.
Personen, die an rheumatischem Fieber mit einer Karditis (Entzündung des Herzens) leiden, entwickeln im späteren Leben möglicherweise Herzkrankheiten und benötigen letztlich einen chirurgischen Eingriff, um die beschädigten Herzklappen zu reparieren.
## Vorsorge
Um ein rheumatisches Fieber zu verhindern, ist es wichtig, bei einer Mandelentzündung einen Arzt aufzusuchen
## Finde mehr über Deine Symptome heraus

# Polimialgia reumática
Escrito pelo nosso [Medical Knowledge Team](https://ada.com/pt/team/medical/)
Atualizado em 15 de fevereiro de 2022 às 10:00 GMT+2
## Nesta página
  * [Visão geral](https://ada.com/pt/conditions/polymyalgia-rheumatica/#visao-geral)
  * [Riscos](https://ada.com/pt/conditions/polymyalgia-rheumatica/#riscos)
  * [Sintomas](https://ada.com/pt/conditions/polymyalgia-rheumatica/#sintomas)
  * [Diagnóstico](https://ada.com/pt/conditions/polymyalgia-rheumatica/#diagnostico)
  * [Tratamento](https://ada.com/pt/conditions/polymyalgia-rheumatica/#tratamento)
  * [Prognóstico](https://ada.com/pt/conditions/polymyalgia-rheumatica/#prognostico)


* * *
Compartilhe esse artigo:
## Visão geral
A polimialgia reumática é uma condição que causa inflamação e dor dos músculos e articulações. A causa é desconhecida. Os sintomas mais comuns são dor muscular e rigidez nos ombros e quadris. A polimialgia reumática tende a ser mais comum em pessoas mais velhas e em mulheres. As pessoas com polimialgia reumática são geralmente tratadas com medicamentos esteróides. Algumas pessoas podem achar que seus sintomas desaparecem após um período de tratamento com medicamentos esteróides, enquanto outras podem ter sintomas constantes ou períodos de recorrência.
## Riscos
Polimialgia reumática é uma condição que causa inflamação e inchaço das articulações e músculos. A causa desta condição não é conhecida, mas pode ser hereditária. Esta condição tende a afetar mulheres mais comumente do que os homens, e afeta maioritariamente pessoas com mais de 50 anos de idade.
## Sintomas
O sintoma mais comum é dor e rigidez matinal em ambos os ombros e quadris. Algumas pessoas notam dificuldade em ficar em pé após sentar-se, ou têm inchaço nos pés ou nas articulações. Além disso, as pessoas com esta condição podem sofrer de desânimo, febre, perda de peso não intencional, suores noturnos e cansaço extremo.
## Diagnóstico
O diagnóstico de polimialgia reumática em geral se baseia nos sintomas e exame clínico. Os exames de sangue geralmente mostram sinais de inflamação no corpo, e também são usados ​​para excluir outras causas possíveis para os sintomas. Um ultra-som das articulações afetadas costuma apresentar inflamação e inchaço da articulação.
## Tratamento
A polimialgia reumática é geralmente tratada com medicamentos esteróides. Estes em geral se tomam regularmente durante 1 ou 2 anos, tempo após o qual os sintomas podem melhorar. Algumas pessoas podem precisar de tomar esses medicamentos por mais tempo. O uso de esteróides por muito tempo pode causar complicações, e estas devem ser conversadas com um médico ou farmacêutico.
## Prognóstico
Medicamentos esteróides geralmente são eficazes na redução dos sintomas. Muitas pessoas com polimialgia reumática relatam que seus sintomas melhoram passado algum tempo com o tratamento. Nesses casos, o tratamento com esteróides pode então ser interrompido. Algumas pessoas sofrem recorrência dos sintomas.

# Friedreich's Ataxia
Written by [Ada’s Medical Knowledge Team](https://ada.com/team/medical/)
Updated on January 20, 2025 at 10:00 AM GMT+2
## On this page
  * [Overview](https://ada.com/conditions/friedreich-ataxia/#overview)
  * [What is Friedreich's ataxia?](https://ada.com/conditions/friedreich-ataxia/#what-is-friedreich-s-ataxia)
  * [Symptoms](https://ada.com/conditions/friedreich-ataxia/#symptoms)
  * [When to see a doctor?](https://ada.com/conditions/friedreich-ataxia/#when-to-see-a-doctor)
  * [Causes](https://ada.com/conditions/friedreich-ataxia/#causes)
  * [Diagnosis](https://ada.com/conditions/friedreich-ataxia/#diagnosis)
  * [Treatments](https://ada.com/conditions/friedreich-ataxia/#treatments)
  * [Complications](https://ada.com/conditions/friedreich-ataxia/#complications)
  * [Wrapping up](https://ada.com/conditions/friedreich-ataxia/#wrapping-up)
  * [FAQs](https://ada.com/conditions/friedreich-ataxia/#faqs)


* * *
Share this article:
## Overview
  * Friedreich’s ataxia is a rare medical condition that affects the nervous system.
  * Friedreich’s ataxia is caused by a genetic mutation that can be passed on from parents to their children. 
  * FA treatment can help manage symptoms and support your daily activities.


Think you might be experiencing Friedreich's ataxia
Friedreich’s ataxia
## What is Friedreich's ataxia?
Friedreich’s ataxia (FA)  rare medical condition affecting the nervous systemgenetic[1](https://ada.com/conditions/friedreich-ataxia/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [2](https://ada.com/conditions/friedreich-ataxia/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2")
## What are Friedreich's ataxia symptoms?
The symptoms of Friedreich’s ataxia affect the nerves and the brain. This leads to issues with coordination, your ability to walk, your muscles and the way you feel things. FA symptoms[1](https://ada.com/conditions/friedreich-ataxia/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [3](https://ada.com/conditions/friedreich-ataxia/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3") [2](https://ada.com/conditions/friedreich-ataxia/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2")
  * Difficulty with muscle coordination
  * Difficulty walking and frequent falling
  * Increasing weakness in the legs
  * Poor balance
  * Loss of sensation of position which usually starts in the arms and legs
  * Loss of normal reflexes
  * Slowness and slurring of speech
  * High muscle tone 
  * Curvature of the spine called scoliosis
  * Difficulty swallowing 
  * Hearing and vision loss
  * Feeling tired
  * Difficulty breathing and palpitations [4](https://ada.com/conditions/friedreich-ataxia/#fn:4 "See Footnote 4")


With FA, these symptoms are known to get worse over time. How quickly the symptoms get worse can be different from person to person. 
Could Friedreich's ataxia explain your symptoms? Don't wait to find out.
## When to see a doctor?
If you are experiencing any of the signs of Friedreich’s ataxiaIf you have a relative with Friedreich’s ataxia
## What causes Friedreich's ataxia?
Friedreich’s ataxia is a genetic condition. It occurs due to a change, or mutation, in the FXN gene. This gene that can be passed along from parents to their children. If you’ve inherited this mutated gene from both parents, then the condition will develop. If you’ve only inherited it from one parent, then you are a carrier of the condition genetic testing[1](https://ada.com/conditions/friedreich-ataxia/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [2](https://ada.com/conditions/friedreich-ataxia/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2")
## How is Friedreich’s ataxia diagnosed?
A Friedreich’s ataxia diagnosis can be made by a physician. Your physician will ask you questions about your symptoms and your medical history physical examdiagnostic tests[1](https://ada.com/conditions/friedreich-ataxia/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [2](https://ada.com/conditions/friedreich-ataxia/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2")
  * Electromyogram (EMG) 
  * Nerve conduction studies 
  * Electrocardiogram (ECG)
  * Echocardiogram 
  * Blood tests
  * Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
  * Computed tomography (CT)


The progression of Friedreich’s ataxia can also be measured 
Are you worried your symptoms might be Friedreich's ataxia? 
## Friedreich’s ataxia treatment options
Friedreich’s ataxia can not be cured.treatment possible to relieve the symptoms and to help Friedreich’s ataxia patients maintain their daily activities as long as possible. 
Friedreich’s ataxia treatment can consist of omaveloxolone[1](https://ada.com/conditions/friedreich-ataxia/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1") [5](https://ada.com/conditions/friedreich-ataxia/#fn:5 "See Footnote 5") [2](https://ada.com/conditions/friedreich-ataxia/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2")
  * Physical therapy
  * **[Diabetes](https://ada.com/conditions/diabetes/) **can be treated if present
  * **[Heart problems](https://ada.com/cardiovascular/) **can be treated if present 
  * Curvatures in the back called scoliosis can be treated with a brace or surgery 
  * Speech therapy
  * Hearing aids


Friedreich’s ataxia is still being studied in order to get a better understanding of the condition and to find new treatment options. 
## Complications of Friedreich’s ataxia
As Friedreich’s ataxia affects the nervous system, it can cause issues with muscle function. As a result of this, a condition called cardiomyopathy diabetes[1](https://ada.com/conditions/friedreich-ataxia/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1")
## Wrapping up
Friedreich’s ataxia is a rare genetic condition which affects the nervous system. It can cause issues with coordination, your ability to use your muscles, and to feel the body's position and movement. Although the condition can not be cured, there are several treatments available which can help improve the symptoms and quality of life of Friedreich’s ataxia patients. 
## Find out more about your symptoms
## Friedreich’s ataxia FAQs
Q: What are the early signs of Friedreich’s ataxia?   
A: Some of the early signs of Friedreich’s ataxia may include issues with coordination, balance, loss of reflexes, slurred speech, scoliosis, fatigue,  
Q: How many people have Friedreich’s ataxia?   
A: Although Friedreich’s ataxia is a rare condition, it is the most common form of inherited ataxia in the U.S. It is estimated that 1 in 50.000 people suffer from the condition worldwide. 
Q: How is Friedreich’s ataxia inherited?   
A: The mutated gene responsible for the development of Friedreich’s ataxia can be passed on from parents to their children. If you have inherited the gene from one parent, then the disease won’t develop, but you will be a carrier, meaning that you can pass the gene along to your children. If you’ve received the gene from both parents, then the condition will develop. 
Q: How is Friedreich’s ataxia diagnosed?  
A: Friedreich’s ataxia can be diagnosed after a physician asks you questions about your medical history and the symptoms you’re experiencing. A physical exam is also necessary and can be followed by additional tests such as nerve conduction studies, blood tests, an MRI, CT, EMG or ECG. 
Q: Is Friedreich’s ataxia fatal?   
A: Friedreich’s ataxia prognosis is often not good, as there is no cure for the condition and it causes heart disease, which is the leading cause of death for people with FA. People with less severe Friedreich’s ataxia can have an average life expectancy of 60 and older.

# COVID-19-Symptom: Corona-Zehen
Verfasst von [Adas medizinischem Fachpersonal](https://ada.com/de/team/medical/)
Aktualisiert am 20. Juni 2025 um 13:44 OESZ
## Auf dieser Seite
  * [Überblick](https://ada.com/de/covid/covid-19-zehen/#ueberblick)
  * [Was sind COVID-Zehen?](https://ada.com/de/covid/covid-19-zehen/#was-sind-covid-zehen)
  * [Ursachen](https://ada.com/de/covid/covid-19-zehen/#ursachen)
  * [Symptome](https://ada.com/de/covid/covid-19-zehen/#symptome)
  * [Dauert](https://ada.com/de/covid/covid-19-zehen/#dauert)
  * [Behandlung](https://ada.com/de/covid/covid-19-zehen/#behandlung)

Artikel teilen:
## Überblick
COVID-Zehen
  * Verfärbte und geschwollene COVID-Zehen gehören zu den seltenen Symptomen einer Coronavirus-Infektion.
  * Bislang ist unklar, welche Ursachen hinter COVID-Zehen stecken. Als mögliche Ursachen vermutet man eine Reaktion auf das Coronavirus oder durch das körpereigene Immunsystem.
  * Kühle Umschläge und verschiedene Medikamente können die Symptome im Zusammenhang mit COVID-Zehen lindern.
  * Meistens verschwinden COVID-Zehen ohne Behandlung nach 10 bis 14 Tagen von selbst.


Finde mehr über Deine Symptome heraus.
## Was sind COVID-Zehen?
Bei COVID-Zehen handelt es sich um eine seltene Hauterkrankung im Zusammenhang mit einer Coronavirus-Infektion. Dabei können eine oder mehrere Zehen anschwellen oder sich verfärben.
Mit der [Ada-App](https://ada.com/de/app/) kannst Du Deine Symptome ganz einfach checken. 
## Welche Ursachen stecken hinter COVID-Zehen?
Derzeit diskutieren medizinische Fachleute, was genau COVID-Zehen verursacht. Sie haben bei Corona-Zehen bereits ein ähnliches Entzündungsmuster wie bei Frostbeulen[1](https://ada.com/de/covid/covid-19-zehen/#fn:1 "See Footnote 1")
Neuere Studien deuten an, dass die Reaktion unseres Immunsystems auf das Coronavirus eine Rolle bei der Entstehung von COVID-Zehen spielen könnte. Während der Körper das Coronavirus bekämpft, kann es zu Entzündungen kommen, die sich in den Zehen zeigen.[2](https://ada.com/de/covid/covid-19-zehen/#fn:2 "See Footnote 2")
Außerdem können einige GrunderkrankungenEntstehung von COVID-Zehen beitragen[wegen einer Coronavirus-Infektion im Krankenhaus behandelt wurden](https://ada.com/de/covid/) und die sich deshalb wenig bewegen konnten.
Einige Forschende nehmen an, dass eine Kombination der oben genannten Faktoren COVID-Zehen verursachen könnte. Diese Vermutung ist jedoch noch nicht bewiesen.
COVID-Zehen können in jedem Alter auftreten. Besonders häufig sind jedoch Kinder, Jugendliche und junge Erwachsene davon betroffen. Diese Personen sind in der Regel gesund und zeigen oft keine oder nur milde [Symptome einer Coronavirus-Infektion](https://ada.com/de/covid/corona-symptome/) wie trockener Husten, Fieber und Muskelschmerzen.[3](https://ada.com/de/covid/covid-19-zehen/#fn:3 "See Footnote 3")
## Wie sehen COVID-Zehen aus?
COVID-Zehen machen sich mit einer Schwellung und Verfärbunganderen Symptomen
  * Schmerzen
  * Juckreiz
  * Bläschen
  * Hautausschläge
  * Geschwüre
  * Trockene oder raue Haut


Die betroffene Stelle kann sich warm anfühlen und ist möglicherweise empfindlich oder schmerzhaft. Manche Menschen mit einer Coronavirus-Infektion berichteten von einem Taubheitsgefühl in den Zehen. In schweren Fällen können COVID-Zehen das Gehen oder Stehen erschweren.
Mit der [Ada-App](https://ada.com/de/app/) kannst Du Deine Symptome ganz einfach checken. 
## Wie lange dauern die COVID-Zehensymptome an?
COVID-Zehen verschwinden meistens ohne Behandlung von allein. Es gibt noch keine verlässlichen Angaben, wie lange diese Erkrankung bei den meisten Menschen anhält. Bei einigen Patient:innen dauerte es 10 bis 14 Tagemehrere Monate
## Wie sieht die Behandlung von Corona-Zehen aus?
Die Behandlung von COVID-ZehenDazu gehören zum Beispiel
  * Hochlagern des Fußes
  * Kalte Umschläge, um die Entzündung zu lindern
  * Bequeme Schuhe tragen, die nicht drücken und die Füße einengen
  * Nach ärztlicher Beratung: Verschiedene Medikamente wie Schmerzmittel, die auch Schwellungen reduzieren, und Antihistaminika gegen den Juckreiz


In schweren Fällen[4](https://ada.com/de/covid/covid-19-zehen/#fn:4 "See Footnote 4")
Wenn COVID-Zehen durch eine Grunderkrankung wie [Diabetes](https://ada.com/de/conditions/diabetes-mellitus-type-2/) oder PAVK verursacht werden, ist es wichtig, diese zugrunde liegenden Erkrankungen zu behandeln, um weitere Komplikationen zu vermeiden, zum Beispiel:
  * bestimmte Medikamenten
  * Änderung des Lebensstils
  * Behandlung zur Verbesserung der Durchblutung


## Das Wichtigste auf einen Blick
Die Hauterkrankung COVID-Zehen kann bei Menschen auftreten, [die sich mit dem Coronavirus infiziert haben](https://ada.com/de/conditions/covid-19/). Corona-Zehen machen sich mit verfärbten, geschwollenen und schmerzhaften Zehen und Füßen bemerkbar. Sie können durch eine Kombination verschiedener Faktoren verursacht werden, darunter das Coronavirus selbst, die Reaktion des Immunsystems auf das Coronavirus und bestimmte Grunderkrankungen.
Die Behandlung von COVID-Zehen hängt von der zugrunde liegenden Ursache und dem Schweregrad ab. Sie reicht von der Linderung der COVID-19-Symptome über die Therapie von Grunderkrankungen bis zur ärztlichen Hilfe in schweren Fällen.
## Finde mehr über Deine Symptome heraus
## Antworten auf häufige Fragen (FAQs)
F: Was kann man gegen COVID-Zehen tun?
A: Die Behandlung von COVID-Zehen hängt vom Schweregrad und den Ursachen ab. Am besten, Du lässt Dich ärztlich beraten, wenn Du COVID-Zehen hast. So können zum Beispiel bestimmte Salben helfen, die Entzündung und Schmerzen zu lindern. Außerdem kannst Du bequeme Schuhe tragen. In schweren Fällen kann Dir Dein:e Ärzt:in Schmerzmittel oder andere Medikamente verschreiben.
F: Was sind die häufigsten Anzeichen und Symptome von COVID-Zehen?
A: Das häufigste Symptom von COVID-Zehen sind rote oder violette Hautveränderungen, meistens an den Seiten oder an den Spitzen der Zehen. Sie können wie kleine Beulen aussehen, die sich bis hin zu größeren und schmerzhaften Blasen entwickeln können. Meistens gehen Corona-Zehen mit Juckreiz und/oder Brennen einher. Manchmal kommt es sogar zu einem Taubheitsgefühl in den Zehen. In schwereren Fällen können auch die Füße anschwellen.
F: Wie lange dauert es, bis COVID-Zehen verheilt sind?
A: Der Heilungsprozess kann von Person zu Person variieren und hängt vom Schweregrad ab. Bei den meisten Menschen dauert es etwa 1 bis 2 Wochen, bis die COVID-Zehen verschwunden sind. In seltenen Fällen können Corona-Zehen monatelang bestehen bleiben.
F: Sind die COVID-Zehen gefährlich?
A: Es gibt keine Hinweise, dass COVID-Zehen tödlich sein können. Du solltest sie aber nicht auf die leichte Schulter nehmen. Sie können auf ein geschwächtes Immunsystem oder andere Grunderkrankungen hinweisen, die unbehandelt zu ernsthaften medizinischen Komplikationen führen können. Am besten, Du lässt Dich sofort ärztlich beraten, wenn Du ungewöhnliche Hautveränderungen oder unerklärliche Ausschläge an Deinen Füßen feststellst.
F: Sind COVID-Zehen ansteckend?
A: Viele Fragen zum Coronavirus sind noch nicht beantwortet, darunter auch, ob Menschen mit COVID-Zehen ansteckend sind. Selbstverständlich sind alle mit einem positiven Corona-Test ansteckend.
